            <span style="letter-spacing:0.8pt;">Letter to Shareholders&#160; </span>
          </div>

        <div style="margin-top:35.2pt;min-height:245pt;margin-left:-18pt;width:207pt;">
          <div style="margin-top:14.2pt; text-align:center; width:207pt; line-height:13pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;font-size:13.03pt;">

          <div style="margin-left:54pt;width:135pt;float:left;">
            <div style="width:135pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;">
              <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">&#8199; </span>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-left:21pt;width:324pt;float:left;">
            <div style="width:324pt; line-height:12pt;color:#000000;">
              <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Dear Fellow Shareholders,</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
            </div>
            <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:324pt; line-height:12pt;">
              <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">2026 has been a year of investment and progress for Tesla. We continued solidifying our foundation by strengthening our core vehicle, energy and services businesses as we build the infrastructure for our next phase of growth.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
            </div>
            <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:324pt; line-height:12pt;">
              <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We also moved closer to a future of autonomous transportation and real-world super intelligence (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #526773 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">SI</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;). This year, we began producing Cybercab at Gigafactory Texas and expanded our Robotaxi service to more U.S. cities. FSD (Supervised) usage grew exponentially as we continued to gain users and expand into new markets. We surpassed over 10 million vehicles delivered, and the Model&#160;Y remains on track to be the best-selling vehicle this year of any kind, globally, as we achieved record deliveries in countries around the world. We launched the Tesla Semi, which will revolutionize the trucking industry, and unveiled the long-awaited Next Gen Roadster. We also made progress in energy generation and storage, with record deployments out of Megafactory Shanghai and production of the new Megapack 3 at our Megafactory in Texas. As SI infrastructure demand increases, energy storage will be critical to expand capacity from the existing grid.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
            </div>
            <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:324pt; line-height:12pt;">
              <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">At the same time, we continued developing the products and investing in the infrastructure required to provide them at scale, including building our Semi factory in Nevada and the first production lines for Optimus, and additional data center capacity to train our SI systems. Our recent investments in battery and chip manufacturing, including our Terafab initiative, will help secure the supply of critical components enabling us to offer products affordably on a mass market basis so that humanity may benefit. We remain focused on managing costs and maintaining the financial strength to support our ambitious long-term goals.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
            </div>
            <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:324pt; line-height:12pt;">
              <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We have accomplished a great deal, but we are still at the early stages of what we believe Tesla can become. Our employees&#8217; innovation, hard work and dedication are essential to realizing that potential and creating lasting value for you, our shareholders. Your confidence in Tesla means a great deal to us, and we take the trust of our shareholders seriously. We listen to you, as your voices and votes help shape our governance and our future. And, as a Board, we want to continue hearing from as many of you as possible.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
            </div>
            <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:324pt; line-height:12pt;">
              <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">That includes retail investors, who face technological barriers to traditional voting. As a result, Tesla recently pioneered the creation of user-friendly practical tools to empower the voices of retail shareholders, which provide a no-fee, investor-directed voting process similar to those currently available to institutional investors. And because we believe all retail voices should be heard across the capital markets, we have made sure the framework supporting enrollment into voluntary retail voting programs would not only be available to Tesla, but to all public companies.</span>
            </div>

We encourage you to choose this e-mail&#160;option, which will allow us to provide you with the information you need in a timelier manner, save us the cost of printing and mailing documents to you and conserve natural resources. Your election to receive proxy materials by e-mail or in printed form by mail will remain in effect until you terminate it.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Year-Round Engagement</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Our Board of Directors (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Board</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) continuously evaluates our corporate governance structure, practices and policies and weighs stakeholder feedback.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Our Board believes that hearing shareholder and stakeholder perspectives is a critical component of our Company&#8217;s success. Our Board oversees the Company&#8217;s regular engagement with our shareholders and is committed to being responsive. The Board maintains an active, year-round dialogue with our shareholders so that the Board and Company management can identify and consider the issues that matter most to our shareholders. This includes focused one-on-one meetings between our Board and institutional shareholders throughout the year that are designed to give shareholders an opportunity to better understand our strategy and governance, and allow our directors to become better informed about our shareholders&#8217; views and concerns. We pursue multiple avenues for shareholder engagement, including by holding video and teleconference meetings with our shareholders, and issuing periodic reports on our activities.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Publishing an Impact Report annually since 2019, where, in response to stakeholder and shareholder feedback, we have continued to provide disclosures on the culture we have built at Tesla, how we engage and aim to retain our employees, progress we are making on driving the sustainability of our business, the efficiency and safety of our products and how we manage risks in the supply chain, among many other topics. Information contained on, or accessible through, our website and in our Impact Report, or any other website or document, is not incorporated in, and is not part of, this proxy statement or any other report or filing we make with the SEC.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Our Board&#8217;s Commitment to Governance</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Our Board believes in maintaining shareholder confidence through, among other things, demonstrating its responsiveness to shareholder feedback and its commitment to corporate governance. As a recent example of our Board&#8217;s responsiveness to shareholders, in 2025, our Board directed management to put forward a proposal to eliminate the supermajority voting requirements in our certificate of formation and bylaws.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In recent years, our Board has repeatedly asked shareholders to vote on binding resolutions to amend our certificate of formation or certificate of incorporation, as applicable, and our bylaws, in each case as in effect from time to time, to reduce director terms and/or to eliminate supermajority voting requirements. However, such amendments have failed to pass each time that the Board proposed them.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Initially, these votes failed due to low shareholder attendance at our annual meetings. As a result, beginning in 2022, we took active steps in an effort to further increase the participation rate of our retail investors through the development of our Shareholder Platform (discussed below), outreach campaigns, direct mailings, one-on-one engagements and through social media channels. The Board determined that, once total shareholder participation reached at least 65% at a shareholder meeting, it would again propose amendments to Tesla&#8217;s certificate of formation and bylaws to </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>

        <div style="margin-top:-12pt;margin-bottom:25.71pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:right; width:487pt; line-height:9pt;font-size:7pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.42pt;">2026 Proxy Statement&#160;&#160;&#160;</span><span style="font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:0.35pt;">5</span>

      <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;background-color:white;overflow:hidden;margin:2pt 0 17.5pt 0;position:relative;box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-bottom:45pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">eliminate supermajority voting requirements, as we disclosed in the proxy materials distributed in connection with our Annual Meeting of Shareholders in 2023 (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">2023 Annual Meeting</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) and 2024 Annual Meeting. In advance of our 2024 Annual Meeting and 2025 Annual Meeting, to further support shareholder participation, we continued to expand our extensive outreach campaigns. Across those campaigns, we conducted, in the aggregate, over 170 meetings and other direct engagements with shareholders. At the 2024 Annual Meeting, our shareholder participation rate surpassed the 65% threshold, and the Board immediately fulfilled its commitment by directing management to put forward a proposal to eliminate the supermajority voting requirements in our certificate of formation and bylaws. We achieved a shareholder participation rate of 73.6% on this proposal at our 2025 Annual Meeting through our shareholder engagement efforts. However, notwithstanding achieving one of our highest shareholder participation rates, our 2025 management proposal to eliminate the supermajority voting requirements in our certificate of formation and bylaws received the support of approximately 39.4% of our total outstanding shares entitled to vote, failing to pass the standard required to approve the proposal. In light of these voting results, the Board determined not to repropose a binding declassification proposal or a binding proposal to eliminate the supermajority voting requirements at this time, but continues to welcome shareholder feedback on this topic through our engagement sessions. Furthermore, as previously discussed, the Board is consistently listening and receptive to taking further governance actions when appropriate.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">At the same time, we will continue our efforts to further increase retail investor participation rates, including through our voluntary retail voting program (see the question entitled &#8220;What is the Voluntary Retail Voting Program?&#8221; under &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Questions and Answers About the 2026 Annual Meeting and Procedural Matters</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below for additional details), and an active communications campaign via our Shareholder Platform and social media channels encouraging retail shareholders to vote their shares.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Shareholder Platform</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In 2022, building on our efforts to enhance engagement among our retail shareholder base, Tesla launched our Shareholder Platform. Any Tesla shareholder, regardless of the size of their holdings, is not only able to sign up to stay informed about investor-related topics such as quarterly filings and event announcements, but also is eligible for selection to participate in in-person Tesla events such as our Cybercab launch event, Model S/X sunset event, the &#8220;We, Robot&#8221; event, Tesla Semi launch event, Investor Day and Cybertruck delivery event. Tesla has one of the largest retail shareholder bases of any public company. Our retail shareholders are incredibly engaged and tend to have a very strong understanding of the Company, and are an important base of feedback for our management and the Board. We will continue to build the system to maximize depth of engagement and reach. Our goal is for every retail shareholder who wants to engage with the Company to have a meaningful framework for interaction through the Shareholder Platform.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Widely-Accessible Hybrid Annual Shareholder Meetings</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Beginning in 2020, we have conducted our annual meetings both in person and online through a live webcast and online shareholder tools. Our online format opens up engagement to all shareholders, regardless of the amount of stock owned or geography, and allows our substantial retail shareholder population to hear directly from our Board and management, as well as to submit questions online. At the same time, due to investor feedback and interest, we continue to also host our meetings in person, so shareholders have the opportunity to engage with our Board and management in person. Due to demand to attend the 2026 Annual Meeting in person, we will hold a lottery to fairly allocate the ability to attend the 2026 Annual Meeting in person. Please see the question entitled &#8220;</span><span style="font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Can I attend the 2026 Annual Meeting?</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; under &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Questions and Answers About the 2026 Annual Meeting and Procedural Matters</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below for additional details.</span>

          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:18pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:16pt;">

          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:17pt;color:#646469;font-size:15pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.27pt;">Tesla Proposal to Elect Three Class&#160;I Directors</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.3pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">General</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tesla&#8217;s Board currently consists of nine members who are divided into three classes with staggered three-year terms. Our bylaws permit the Board to establish by resolution the authorized number of directors, and nine directors are currently authorized. Any increase or decrease in the number of directors will be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as possible, each class will consist of an equal number of directors. The Board and the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee evaluate the optimal size and composition of the Board on an ongoing basis, taking into account the operations and responsibilities of the Board and the expertise and experience of its membership.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">

Biographical information about each of the nominees is contained in the following section. A discussion of the qualifications, attributes and skills of each nominee that led the Board and the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee to the conclusion that he or she should be elected or continue to serve as a director follows each of the director and nominee biographies.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

Musk and Straubel and Ms.&#160;Denholm. Each of Messrs. Musk and Straubel and Ms.&#160;Denholm has accepted such nomination; however, in the event that a nominee is unable or declines to serve as a director at the time of the 2026 Annual Meeting, the proxies will be voted for any nominee who shall be designated by the Board to fill such vacancy. If you wish to give specific instructions with respect to the voting of directors, you may do so by indicating your instructions on your proxy card or when you vote by telephone or over the Internet. If you are a beneficial owner holding your shares in street name and you do not give voting instructions to your broker, bank or other intermediary, that organization will leave your shares unvoted on this matter.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">As our Chief Executive Officer, one of our founders and our largest shareholder, Mr.&#160;Musk brings historical knowledge, operational and technical expertise and continuity to the Board. Mr.&#160;Musk guided Tesla from an early-stage startup, through its IPO in 2010, to transformative growth into one of the most valuable companies in the world. Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s leadership and unique vision to build the world&#8217;s next generation of sustainable and accessible innovation has played a key role in our mission to build a world of amazing abundance. </span>

                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:6pt; line-height:12pt;font-weight:bold;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Career Highlights</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:3pt; line-height:12pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Mr.&#160;Musk is the Technoking of Tesla and has served as our Chief Executive Officer since October&#160;2008. Mr.&#160;Musk has also served as Chief Executive Officer, Chief Technical Officer and Chairman of Space Exploration Technologies Corporation, a company which develops and launches advanced rockets and spacecraft (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">SpaceX</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), since May&#160;2002 and served as Chairman of the Board of SolarCity Corporation, a solar installation company (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">SolarCity</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), from July&#160;2006 until its acquisition by us in November&#160;2016. He has served as Chief Technology Officer and on the Board of X Corp., a social media company (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">X</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), since October&#160;2022, and has served as the Chief Executive Officer and on the Board of X.AI Corp., an artificial intelligence company (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">xAI</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), since March&#160;2023, in each case through the March&#160;2025 merger of X and xAI. Following the March&#160;2025 merger of X and xAI, he served as the President, Treasurer and Chief Executive Officer and on the board of directors of X.AI Holdings Corp. (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">xAI&#160;Holdings</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), which later became a subsidiary of SpaceX in February&#160;2026. Mr.&#160;Musk is also a founder of The Boring Company (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">TBC</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), an infrastructure company, and Neuralink Corp., a company focused on developing brain-machine interfaces, where he serves as the Chief Executive Officer. Prior to SpaceX, Mr.&#160;Musk co-founded PayPal, an electronic payment system, which was acquired by eBay in October&#160;2002, and Zip2 Corporation, a provider of Internet enterprise software and services, which was acquired by Compaq in March&#160;1999. Mr.&#160;Musk also served on the board of directors of Endeavor Group Holdings, Inc. from April&#160;2021 to June&#160;2022.</span>

She also founded TreeArc Investment Group in 2021, with a mission to invest in ventures that deliver a positive impact. The firm&#8217;s investment portfolio spans environmental, venture capital and community-focused investments, and includes majority ownership in two professional basketball teams, the Sydney Kings and Sydney Flames, and majority ownership of the Women&#8217;s National Basketball League in Australia. From January&#160;2017 through June&#160;2019, Ms.&#160;Denholm was with Telstra Corporation Limited, a telecommunications company (&#8220;Telstra&#8221;), where she served as Chief Financial Officer and Head of Strategy from October&#160;2018 through June&#160;2019, and Chief Operations Officer from January&#160;2017 to October&#160;2018. Prior to Telstra, from August&#160;2007 to July&#160;2016, Ms.&#160;Denholm was with Juniper Networks, Inc., a manufacturer of networking equipment, serving in executive roles including Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operations Officer. Prior to joining Juniper Networks, Ms.&#160;Denholm served in various executive roles at Sun Microsystems, Inc. from January&#160;1996 to August&#160;2007. Ms.&#160;Denholm also served at Toyota Motor Corporation Australia for seven&#160;years and at Arthur Andersen &amp; Company for five&#160;years in various finance assignments. Ms.&#160;Denholm previously served as a director of ABB Ltd. Ms.&#160;Denholm is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Australia/New Zealand, a member of the Australian Institute of Company Directors, and holds a Bachelor&#8217;s degree in Economics from the University of Sydney and a Master&#8217;s degree in Commerce and a Doctor of Business Administration (honoris causa) from the University of New South Wales.</span>

Mr.&#160;Ehrenpreis&#8217; tenure on Tesla&#8217;s Board also provides the Company with stability and experience as it navigates through different challenges.</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:6pt; line-height:12pt;font-weight:bold;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Career Highlights</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:6pt; line-height:12pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Mr.&#160;Ehrenpreis has been a venture capitalist since 1996. He is a founder and managing member of DBL Partners, a leading impact investing venture capital firm formed in 2015. Previously, he led the Energy Innovation practice at Technology Partners. Mr.&#160;Ehrenpreis has served on the board and Executive Committee, including as Annual Meeting Chairman of the National Venture Capital Association (NVCA). Mr.&#160;Ehrenpreis currently serves as the Chairman of the VCNetwork, the largest and most active California venture capital organization, and as the President of the Western Association of Venture Capitalists (WAVC), the oldest venture capital organization in California. Mr.&#160;Ehrenpreis is also deeply involved in the energy technology sector. He currently serves on the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) Advisory Council, the University of Texas at Austin Energy Institute Advisory Board, and the Stanford Precourt Institute for Energy Advisory Council, and has served on the advisory boards of many industry groups, including the American Council on Renewable Energy, the Cleantech Venture Network (Past Chairman of Advisory Board) and the Stanford Global Climate and Energy Project (GCEP). He was also Chairman of the Clean-Tech Investor Summit for nine&#160;years. Mr.&#160;Ehrenpreis served for&#160;years as the Chairman of the Silicon Valley Innovation &amp; Entrepreneurship Forum (SVIEF) and on the Advisory Board of the Forum for Women Entrepreneurs (FWE). Ms.&#160;Wilson-Thompson has served on the board of directors of Wolverine World Wide, Inc. since May&#160;2021 and McKesson Corporation since January&#160;2022. She has also served on the board of directors of Health Care Service Corporation since October&#160;2024. Ms.&#160;Wilson-Thompson holds an A.B. in English Literature from the University of Michigan and a J.D. and LL.M. (Corporate and Finance Law) from Wayne State University.</span>
                    </div>
                  </td>

          <div style="margin-top:-3pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Additional Information</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;font-size:9.85pt;">
            <span style="font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:0.591pt;">On October&#160;16, 2018, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:0.591pt;">New York Court</span><span style="font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:0.591pt;">&#8221;) entered a final judgment approving the terms of a settlement filed with the New York Court on September&#160;29, 2018, in connection with the actions taken by the SEC relating to Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s August&#160;7, 2018 Twitter (now known as X) post that he was considering taking Tesla private. On April&#160;26, 2019, this settlement was amended to clarify certain of its terms, which amendment was subsequently approved by the New York Court. Mr.&#160;Musk did not admit to or deny any of the SEC&#8217;s allegations, and there is no restriction on Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s ability to serve as an officer or director on the Board.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;font-size:10pt;">&#8203;<span style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span></span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">On April&#160;3, 2026, in </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Pampena v. Musk</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California entered a partial judgment against Mr.&#160;Musk in his personal capacity only in favor of lead plaintiffs on behalf of themselves and a class of investors who sold certain Twitter, Inc. equity securities between May&#160;13 and October&#160;4, 2022. The judgment is based on a jury verdict rendered on March&#160;20,&#160;2026 that found (i)&#160;in favor of plaintiffs on claims alleging that Mr.&#160;Musk violated Section&#160;10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule&#160;10b-5(b) thereunder in connection with two statements made by Mr.&#160;Musk in May&#160;2022, and (ii)&#160;in favor of Mr.&#160;Musk on claims challenging a third statement and alleging a &#8220;scheme to defraud&#8221; under Rules 10b-5(a) and (c). On July 6, 2026, the court entered an order granting Mr. Musk&#8217;s motion for judgment as a matter of law as to one of the two statements for which lead plaintiffs had obtained the jury verdict in their favor and denying the remainder of Mr. Musk&#8217;s motion. On July 30, 2026, Mr. Musk filed a notice of appeal to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, which appeal remains pending. The partial judgment remains subject to that appeal and any subsequent proceedings. The claims in this case all concern Mr. Musk&#8217;s then-pending potential purchase of Twitter, Inc.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:4pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;font-style:italic;">

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-bottom:51pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:18pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:16pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.8pt;">Proposal Two </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:17pt;color:#646469;font-size:15pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.27pt;">Tesla Proposal for a Non-Binding Advisory Vote Approving 2025 Executive Compensation</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.3pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Background on Required Advisory Vote on Executive Compensation for Prior Fiscal Year</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Pursuant to Section&#160;14A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Exchange Act</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), we are asking our shareholders to vote to approve, on a non-binding advisory basis, the compensation of our named executive officers (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">NEOs</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) for our prior completed fiscal year, 2025, as disclosed in accordance with the SEC&#8217;s rules in the &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; section of this proxy statement on page <a href="#tECFF">36</a> through page <a href="#tECPI">64</a> below. This proposal, commonly known as a &#8220;say-on-pay&#8221; proposal, gives our shareholders the opportunity to weigh in on our NEOs&#8217; 2025 compensation as a whole. This vote is not intended to address any specific item of compensation for 2025 or any specific NEO, but rather the overall compensation of all of our NEOs for 2025 and the philosophy, policies and practices for our NEOs&#8217; compensation in 2025 described in this proxy statement. We currently include this advisory vote on an annual basis.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The say-on-pay vote is advisory, and therefore not binding on the Company, the Compensation Committee or the Board. The say-on-pay vote will, however, provide information to us regarding investor sentiment about our executive compensation philosophy, policies and practices for future NEO compensation, which the Compensation Committee will be able to consider when determining future executive compensation. The Board and the Compensation Committee value the opinions of our shareholders and to the extent there is any significant vote against our NEOs&#8217; 2025 compensation as disclosed in the section of this proxy statement titled &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; &#8203;(on page <a href="#tECFF">36</a> through page <a href="#tECPI">64</a> below), we will consider our shareholders&#8217; concerns, and the Compensation Committee will evaluate whether any actions are necessary to address those concerns.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Summary of the 2025 Executive Compensation Program</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The following is a summary of some of the key points of our 2025 executive compensation program that are subject to this proposal:</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tesla continued to emphasize structuring compensation incentives to reward our NEOs based on performance.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Equity awards weighed heavily in our NEOs&#8217; total compensation, including awards that vest upon the achievement of clear and measurable milestones. Since these awards increase in value as our stock price increases (and in the case of stock option awards, have no value unless our stock price increases following their grant), our NEOs&#8217; incentives were closely aligned with the long-term interests of our shareholders. From 2020 to 2025, equity awards granted to our NEOs (other than our Chief Executive Officer) had primarily been in the form of stock options: Xiaotong (Tom) Zhu, our Senior Vice President, APAC and Global Vehicle Manufacturing, received 100% of his equity award in the form of stock option awards upon his promotion to such role in 2023, and Vaibhav Taneja, our Chief Financial Officer, received approximately 80% of his equity award in the form of stock options in 2024, following the 2024 review of our compensation programs and in consideration of his promotion in August&#160;2023 to the role of Chief Financial Officer. As a result, a significant portion of our NEOs&#8217; total compensation was entirely at risk, depending on long-term stock price performance. The 2025 CEO Performance Award, while granted in the form of restricted stock, has elements that also provide that Mr. Musk receives no value unless our stock price increases following grant.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:0pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">

            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tesla had no cash bonus program for any of our NEOs and generally did not provide any perquisites or tax reimbursements to our NEOs not available to other employees. No NEO currently has any severance or change of control arrangement, other than certain terminations of employment and change of control provisions in the 2025 CEO Performance Award and the Implementation Agreement as described in &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025 &#8212; Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change in Control as of December 31, 2025,&#8221;</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation &#8212; Equity Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 CEO Performance Award&#8221; and &#8220;Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation &#8212; Historical Equity Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2018 CEO Performance Award.&#8221;</span><span style="font-style:normal;color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>

          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Each NEO was employed at will and was expected to demonstrate exceptional personal performance in order to continue serving as a member of the executive team.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Mr.&#160;Musk, our Chief Executive Officer, historically earned a base salary that reflected the applicable minimum wage requirements under California law, and he was subject to income taxes based on such base salary. However, he has never accepted his salary. Commencing in May&#160;2019 at Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s request, we eliminated altogether the earning and accrual of this base salary.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Mr. Musk received no compensation in 2025 other than the 2025 CEO Interim Award (as defined and discussed below), which was forfeited in its entirety in 2026, and the 2025 CEO Performance Award. The 2025 CEO Performance Award consists of 12 equal tranches, the shares subject to each of which will become &#8220;Earned Shares&#8221; only upon the achievement of a market capitalization milestone and one of 12 operational milestones relating to strategic product goals or Adjusted EBITDA. While our shareholders benefit from each incremental increase in Tesla&#8217;s performance and stock price, aligning their interests with Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s incentives, the Earned Shares subject to each tranche will vest only upon the full achievement of specific milestones, making it even more challenging for Mr.&#160;Musk to realize value from such increases. As of the date of this proxy statement, none of the tranches has become Earned Shares or has vested. Additionally, Mr. Musk must hold the shares for five years after they become Earned Shares, subject to certain limited exceptions. </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">See</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#160;&#8212; Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below for more details.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">For detailed information about Tesla&#8217;s executive compensation program, </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">see</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> the &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; section on page <a href="#tECFF">36</a> through page <a href="#tECPI">64</a> below. </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8220;Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Historical Equity Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2018 CEO Performance Award&#8221;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> on page <a href="#tCOPA">46</a> also discusses the Company&#8217;s entry into the Implementation Agreement after the end of the fiscal year (in April 2026), which agreement implemented a process for Mr. Musk&#8217;s exercise of the vested stock options under the 10-year performance-based stock option award granted to him in January 2018 (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">2018 CEO Performance Award</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), including the imposition of a service-based vesting condition on the shares issued to Mr. Musk upon exercise.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tesla believes that the information provided above and within the &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; section of this proxy statement (on page <a href="#tECFF">36</a> through page <a href="#tECPI">64</a> below) demonstrates that Tesla&#8217;s executive compensation program for fiscal year 2025 was designed appropriately and aligned management&#8217;s interests with our shareholders&#8217; interests to support long-term value creation. </span>
          </div>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.8pt;">Proposal Three</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.32pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:16.5pt;color:#646469;font-size:15pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.27pt;">Tesla Proposal for the Ratification of the Appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as Tesla&#8217;s Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm for the Fiscal Year Ending December&#160;31, 2026</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.3pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">General</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Audit Committee has selected PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as Tesla&#8217;s independent registered public accounting firm to audit the consolidated financial statements of Tesla for the fiscal year ending December&#160;31, 2026, which will include an audit of the effectiveness of Tesla&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP has audited Tesla&#8217;s financial statements since 2005. A representative of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP is expected to be present at the 2026 Annual Meeting, will have the opportunity to make a statement if he or she desires to do so and is expected to be available to respond to appropriate questions from shareholders.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Shareholder ratification of the selection of our independent registered public accounting firm is a matter of good corporate practice. In the event that this selection is not ratified by the affirmative vote of a majority of voting power of Tesla&#8217;s shares present in person or by proxy at the 2026 Annual Meeting and entitled to vote on the subject matter, the appointment of the independent registered public accounting firm will be reconsidered by the Audit Committee. Even if the selection is ratified, the Audit Committee in its discretion may direct the appointment of a different accounting firm at any time during the year if the Audit Committee determines that such a change would be in the best interests of Tesla and our shareholders.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">Audit Fees consist of fees for professional services rendered for the audit of Tesla&#8217;s consolidated financial statements included in Tesla&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K and for the review of the financial statements included in Tesla&#8217;s Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, as well as services that generally only Tesla&#8217;s independent registered public accounting firm can reasonably provide, including statutory audits and services rendered in connection with SEC filings.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.16pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:10pt; margin-top:3.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:16pt;white-space:nowrap;font-size:8pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">(2)</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:3.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:10pt; text-align:left; margin-left:16pt;font-size:8pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">Audit-Related Fees in 2024 and 2025 consisted of fees for professional services for certain agreed upon procedures and other attestation services.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.16pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:10pt; margin-top:3.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:16pt;white-space:nowrap;font-size:8pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">(3)</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:3.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:10pt; text-align:left; margin-left:16pt;font-size:8pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">Tax Fees in 2024 and 2025 consisted of fees related to consultation, tax planning and compliance services.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.16pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:10pt; margin-top:3.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:16pt;white-space:nowrap;font-size:8pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">(4)</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:3.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:10pt; text-align:left; margin-left:16pt;font-size:8pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">Other Fees in 2024 and 2025 consisted of permitted services other than those that meet the criteria above and include fees for accounting research software, the assessment of non-financial metrics and documentation and pre-implementation review of non-financial systems.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.16pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Pre-Approval of Audit and Non-Audit Services</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tesla&#8217;s Audit Committee has adopted a policy for pre-approving audit and non-audit services and associated fees of Tesla&#8217;s independent registered public accounting firm. Under this policy, the Audit Committee must pre-approve all services and associated fees provided to Tesla by its independent registered public accounting firm, with certain de minimis exceptions described in the policy.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>

          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:18pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:16pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.8pt;">Corporate Governance</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.32pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Succession Planning</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Board regularly discusses management succession planning and leadership development in meetings and executive sessions at both the Board and Committee levels. The Board continues to maintain full confidence in Mr. Musk&#8217;s leadership, commitment and vision to guide Tesla through its next strategic chapter of innovation and growth. As a matter of best practice, and to ensure the resiliency of Tesla, the Board regularly considers succession planning for both sudden, unanticipated events, and longer-term planned succession for its executives. Directors regularly interact and engage with not only senior management talent and potential successors to executive management positions, but also high-potential talent throughout the Company, thus providing them with important exposure opportunities. This engagement occurs in Board meetings held throughout the year, as well as through informal events and updates, and regular one-on-one touchpoints.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">As described in our Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee Charter and Corporate Governance Guidelines, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee periodically reviews succession planning for the Chief Executive Officer and other executive officers, reporting its findings and recommendations to the Board and working with the Board in evaluating potential successors to these executive management positions. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee also provides oversight, input and recommendations regarding the criteria to be used for identification of potential candidates for succession to leadership positions. In addition to management succession planning, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee periodically reviews the succession planning for the Board and key leadership roles on the Board, reporting its findings and recommendations to the Board in evaluating potential successors to those positions. In addition, the Compensation Committee is responsible for evaluating the Company&#8217;s talent pipelines and succession planning framework, which encompasses both short-term and long-term strategies for the identification, mentoring, development, retention and replacement of senior leaders. While the Board prioritizes internal candidates for succession planning, and believes that management has developed a robust pipeline of seasoned leadership talent within Tesla, it also monitors exceptional external talent when appropriate.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Director Education</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Director education about Tesla and our industry is an ongoing process that begins when a director joins the Board. Upon joining the Board, new directors are provided with a comprehensive orientation about Tesla, including Tesla&#8217;s business and strategy. The orientation program includes written materials, oral presentations and meetings with senior members of management. The Board believes that ongoing education is important for maintaining a current and effective Board. Accordingly, the Board encourages directors to participate in ongoing education, including accredited director education programs. Furthermore, the Board is proactive regarding the design and content of director education programming. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee is responsible for overseeing the director orientation program and evaluating and making recommendations for continuing education activities of Board members.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Code of Business Ethics and Corporate Governance Guidelines</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Board sets high standards for Tesla&#8217;s workforce, officers and directors. Tesla is committed to establishing an operating framework that exercises appropriate oversight of responsibilities at all levels throughout the Company and managing its affairs in a manner consistent with rigorous principles of business ethics. Accordingly, Tesla has adopted a Code of Business Ethics, which was amended in April&#160;2024, and which is applicable to the directors, officers and personnel of Tesla and its subsidiaries. The Code of Business Ethics sets forth Tesla&#8217;s guiding principles, which include thinking before acting, treating everyone with respect, protecting our information and assets and doing business with integrity. For more information on how we support our employees and our commitment to integrity and respect, please refer to the People and Community section of our 2025 Impact Report. Tesla has also adopted Corporate Governance Guidelines, which, in conjunction with our certificate of formation, bylaws and charters of the standing committees of the Board, form the framework for Tesla&#8217;s corporate governance.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
        </div>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.35pt;">24</span><span style="font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.42pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;2026 Proxy Statement</span>

      <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;background-color:white;overflow:hidden;margin:2pt 0 17.5pt 0;position:relative;box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:23.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="margin-top:17pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Code of Business Ethics and the Corporate Governance Guidelines are each available on Tesla&#8217;s website at: http://ir.tesla.com/corporate. Tesla will disclose on its website any amendment to the Code of Business Ethics, as well as any waivers of the Code of Business Ethics, that are required to be disclosed by the rules of the SEC or Nasdaq.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Director Independence</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Board periodically assesses, with the recommendation of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, the independence of its members as defined in the listing standards of Nasdaq and applicable law. The Board undertook an analysis for each director and director nominee and considered all relevant facts and circumstances, including the director&#8217;s other commercial, accounting, legal, banking, consulting, charitable and familial relationships. The Board determined that with respect to each of its current members and director nominees, other than Mr.&#160;Musk, who is our Chief Executive Officer, and Mr.&#160;Kimbal Musk, who is Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s brother, there are no disqualifying factors with respect to director independence enumerated in the listing standards of Nasdaq or any relationships that would interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out the responsibilities of a director, and that each such member is an &#8220;independent director&#8221; as defined in the listing standards of Nasdaq and applicable laws.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In particular, the Board reviewed the following considerations:</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6.2pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Ira Ehrenpreis, Joe Gebbia, Jack Hartung, James Murdoch, Mr.&#160;Musk, Mr.&#160;Kimbal Musk, JB&#160;Straubel and/or investment funds managed by or otherwise affiliated with any of the foregoing have made minority investments in, and/or may serve as independent directors of, certain companies or investment funds (i)&#160;of which other Tesla directors are founders, significant shareholders, directors, officers, managers or affiliates and/or (ii)&#160;with which Tesla has had certain relationships, such as those set forth in &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Related Person Transactions</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">.&#8221; The Board concluded that none of these relationships are material so as to impede the exercise of independent judgment by any of Messrs. Ehrenpreis, Gebbia, Hartung, Murdoch or Straubel.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Board Leadership Structure</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Roles of Chair of the Board</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Following careful deliberation, the Board appointed Robyn Denholm to serve as the independent Chair of the Board in November&#160;2018, having considered her strong leadership, independent presence and financial and business expertise on the Board over an extended period of time. Together, Ms.&#160;Denholm and our Chief Executive Officer, Mr.&#160;Musk, comprise our senior Board leadership, which the Board continues to believe is appropriate at this time. As Chair of the Board, Ms.&#160;Denholm has broad authority and oversight over the affairs of the Board, with Mr.&#160;Musk available to her as a resource in this regard. Moreover, as an independent Chair of the Board, Ms.&#160;Denholm has the authority to coordinate the actions of the other independent directors and regularly communicate, as their representative, with Mr.&#160;Musk.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">As Chair of the Board, Ms.&#160;Denholm, among other things:</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Reviews the agenda and materials for meetings of the independent directors;</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Consults with our Chief Executive Officer regarding Board meeting agendas, schedules and materials;</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>

          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tesla also has a mechanism for shareholders to communicate directly with non-management directors (</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">see</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Corporate Governance&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Contacting the Board</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below).</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Committees of the Board</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In addition, the Board has four standing committees&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;the Audit Committee, the Compensation Committee, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and the Disclosure Controls Committee&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;which are each further described below. Each of the Committees consists solely of independent directors, and the Board may appoint a chair of each Committee. Our independent directors regularly meet in executive session and at such other times as necessary or appropriate as determined by the independent directors. In addition, as part of our governance review and succession planning, the Board (led by the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee) evaluates our leadership structure to ensure that it remains the optimal structure for Tesla and fosters sufficient depth and experience to support its continued growth and execution of its long-term strategies, reviews the composition, size and performance of the Board and its Committees, evaluates individual Board members and identifies and evaluates candidates to fill vacancies on the Board and for election or re-election to the Board. </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">See</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Corporate Governance&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Process and Considerations for Nominating Board Candidates</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below for additional information.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Board Role in Risk Oversight</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Board is responsible for overseeing the major risks facing Tesla while management is responsible for assessing and mitigating Tesla&#8217;s risks on a day-to-day basis. The Board is assisted by our Committees, which consist entirely of independent directors, and which report to the Board as appropriate on matters that involve specific areas of risk that each Committee oversees.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

                <td style="padding:0pt; width:6pt;">&#8203;</td>
                <td colspan="4" style="padding:0.567pt 0pt 4.6pt 0pt; width:0pt;">
                  <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Compensation Committee oversees management of risks relating to Tesla&#8217;s compensation plans and programs. Tesla&#8217;s management and the Compensation Committee have assessed the risks associated with Tesla&#8217;s compensation policies and practices for all employees, including non-executive officers. These include risks relating to setting ambitious targets for our employees&#8217; compensation or the vesting of their equity awards, our emphasis on at-risk equity-based compensation and the potential impact of such practices on the retention or decision-making of our employees, particularly our senior management. Based on the results of this assessment, Tesla does not believe that its compensation policies and practices for all employees, including non-executive officers, create risks that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on Tesla.</span>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We have a highly effective and engaged Board. As illustrated by the chart above, our Board and its Committees met, on average, more than once per week in 2025, and the number of meetings held by each of the Board, Audit Committee and Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee was above the corresponding average number of meetings across the S&amp;P 500.</span><span style=" position:relative; bottom:4.25pt;font-size:7.5pt;letter-spacing:0.45pt;">(1)</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> While we do not maintain a numerical limit on public company boards our directors may serve on, our Corporate Governance Guidelines provide that each member is expected to ensure that other existing and future commitments, including employment responsibilities and service on the boards of other entities, do not materially interfere with the member&#8217;s service to us as a director. When conducting its annual review of the effectiveness and productivity of its members, the Board evaluates many factors, including without limitation, the director&#8217;s attendance at meetings, the participation and input of the director and the director&#8217;s preparation at meetings.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Chair of the Board and Committee Chairs provide additional independent leadership outside the boardroom.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">For example, each Committee Chair determines the frequency and length of, and develops the agenda for, their respective Committee meetings. This includes providing feedback on the form and type of related materials, considering whether the relevant Committee is appropriately carrying out its core responsibilities and focusing on the key issues facing Tesla. In carrying out these responsibilities, each Committee Chair engages with key members of management and subject matter experts as preparation in advance of each Committee meeting. In 2025, Robyn Denholm and Ira Ehrenpreis, in carrying out their duties as Committee Chairs, participated in over 100 meetings, including with Company management and independent consultants and auditors.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

In 2025, Robyn Denholm, in carrying out her role as Chair of the Board, participated in over 100 meetings, including with shareholders, Company management and independent consultants. As discussed above, the Chair of the Board and Committee Chairs are proactive about preparing for meetings, which enables the Board and its Committees to delve into the details of the issues facing Tesla and reinforces a nuanced understanding of our business.</span>

                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Disclosure Controls Committee has adopted a written charter approved by the Board, which is available on Tesla&#8217;s website at: http://ir.tesla.com/corporate.</span>
                    </div>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Robyn Denholm, Ira Ehrenpreis and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson served as members of the Compensation Committee during 2025. None of such persons is or was formerly an officer or an employee of Tesla. </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">See</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Related Person Transactions</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below for certain transactions involving Tesla in which members of the Compensation Committee may potentially be deemed to have an indirect interest.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
