          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Process and Considerations for Nominating Board Candidates</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee is responsible for, among other things, determining the criteria for Board membership, recommending Board candidates and proposing any changes to the composition of the Board. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee&#8217;s criteria and process for fulfilling these duties are generally as follows:</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.9pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:5.9pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee regularly reviews the current composition, size and tenure of the Board, and oversees an annual evaluation of the performance of the Board as a whole and of its individual members. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee applies uniform evaluation processes and standards for all Board members, including in identifying, considering or recommending new candidates for the Board to fill vacancies or add additional directors and in recommending existing Board members for nomination to be re-elected at annual meetings of shareholders.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>

            <!--blacklining:none;-->

          <div style="margin-left:10pt; width:477pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">on the Board. While the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee has not established specific minimum qualifications for director candidates, it considers all pertinent factors that it considers appropriate, and believes that the Board should consist of directors who (i)&#160;are, in the majority, independent, (ii)&#160;are of high integrity, (iii)&#160;have broad, business-related knowledge and experience at the policy-making level in business or technology, including their understanding of Tesla&#8217;s business in particular, (iv)&#160;have qualifications that will increase overall Board effectiveness, (v)&#160;represent diversity of professional experience and (vi)&#160;meet other requirements as may be required by applicable rules, such as financial literacy or financial expertise with respect to Audit Committee members. For example, after conducting independent director searches from time to time in which numerous highly qualified candidates from a variety of backgrounds were considered, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee recommended to the Board Joe Gebbia as a director in 2022, JB Straubel as a director in 2023 and Jack Hartung as a director in 2025, to further bolster the Board&#8217;s expertise in technological innovation, public company management, financial reporting and sustainability initiatives.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In evaluating and identifying candidates, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee has the authority to retain and terminate any third-party search firm that is used to identify director candidates and has the authority to approve the fees and retention terms of any search firm.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">With regard to any candidates who are properly recommended by shareholders (as described in more detail below) or by other sources, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee will review the qualifications of any such candidate, which review may, in the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee&#8217;s discretion, include interviewing references for the candidate, direct interviews with the candidate or other actions that the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee deems necessary or proper.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">After completing its review and evaluation of director candidates, the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee recommends the director nominees that it has determined to be qualified to the full Board.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">It is the policy of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee to consider properly submitted recommendations for candidates to the Board from shareholders. Shareholder recommendations for candidates to the Board must be directed in writing to Tesla, Inc., 1 Tesla Road, Austin, Texas 78725, Attention: Legal Department, and should also be sent by e-mail to shareholdermail@tesla.com. Such recommendations must include the candidate&#8217;s name, home and business contact information, detailed biographical data and qualifications, information regarding any relationships between the candidate and Tesla within the last three&#160;years and evidence of the nominating person&#8217;s ownership of Tesla stock. Such recommendations must also include a statement from the recommending shareholder in support of the candidate, particularly within the context of the criteria for Board membership, including issues of character, integrity, judgment, age, independence, skills, education, expertise, business acumen, business experience, length of service, understanding of Tesla&#8217;s business, other commitments and the like, as well as any personal references and an indication of the candidate&#8217;s willingness to serve.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Attendance at Annual Meetings of Shareholders by the Board</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Although Tesla does not have a formal policy regarding attendance by members of the Board at Tesla&#8217;s annual meetings of shareholders, directors are encouraged to attend. All of our directors attended the 2025 Annual Meeting.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Stock Transactions</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Hedging, Short Sales and Rule&#160;10b5-1 Trading Plans</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;"> <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" format="ixt:fixed-true" name="ecd:InsiderTrdPoliciesProcAdoptedFlag" id="ixv-13356">Tesla has an insider trading policy</ix:nonNumeric> that is reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws, rules and regulations and Nasdaq listing standards. The insider trading policy prohibits all of our directors, officers and employees from, among other things, engaging in short sales, hedging or similar transactions designed to decrease the risks associated with holding Tesla securities. This prohibition encompasses transactions in publicly traded options, such as puts and </span> </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">

      <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;background-color:white;overflow:hidden;margin:2pt 0 17.5pt 0;position:relative;box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">calls, and other derivative securities with respect to Tesla securities, but not transactions designed to facilitate portfolio diversification, such as broad-based index options, futures or baskets. It is also the policy of Tesla to comply with all applicable securities laws when transacting in its own securities. A copy of the insider trading policy is filed as Exhibit 19 to Tesla&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Stock Ownership by the Board and Management</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">To align the interests at the highest level of our management with those of our shareholders, the Board has instituted the following requirements relating to stock ownership under our Corporate Governance Guidelines.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Each member of the Board and all of our NEOs are subject to the following minimum stock ownership requirements: (i) each director is required to own shares of Tesla stock equal in value to at least five times the annual cash retainer for directors (regardless of whether or not the retainer has been waived, and exclusive of retainer amounts for service as a member or chair of a Board committee) and (ii)&#160;our NEOs are required to own shares of Tesla stock equal in value to at least six times his/her base salary; provided that equity-based awards are not counted under Tesla&#8217;s Stock Ownership Guidelines. Each individual shall have five&#160;years from the date such person assumed his or her relevant role at Tesla to come into compliance with these requirements. Each person&#8217;s compliance with the minimum stock ownership level will be determined on the date when this compliance grace period expires, and then annually on each December&#160;31, by multiplying the number of shares held by such person and the average closing price of those shares during the preceding month. Our NEOs and each of our directors are currently either in compliance with these requirements or are in the applicable period to come into compliance therewith.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Pursuant to our Corporate Governance Guidelines, no equity award as to which vesting or the lapse of a period of restriction occurs based solely on the passage of time that is granted to any NEO may vest, or have a period of restriction that lapses, earlier than six months from the date on which such vesting or lapse commences. Furthermore, our Corporate Governance Guidelines provide that no NEO may sell, transfer, pledge, assign or otherwise dispose of any shares of Tesla stock acquired pursuant to any stock option, restricted stock unit or other equity award granted by Tesla earlier than the date that is six&#160;months after the date on which such award vests or the period of restriction with respect to such award lapses, as applicable.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Prohibition of Equity Award Repricing</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tesla views equity-based compensation to be a key factor in incentivizing the future performance of our personnel. Consequently, the amended and restated 2019 Equity Incentive Plan of Tesla, Inc. (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">A&amp;R 2019 Equity Incentive Plan</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) provides, and Tesla&#8217;s previous 2010 Equity Incentive Plan provided, that stock options and other equity awards issued under these plans that derive their value from the appreciation of the value of Tesla&#8217;s stock may not be exchanged for other awards, repurchased for cash or otherwise be made the subject of transactions that have the purpose or effect of repricing such awards. The A&amp;R 2019 Equity Incentive Plan prohibits repricing.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Contacting the Board</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Any shareholder who desires to contact our non-employee directors regarding appropriate Tesla business-related comments may do so electronically at the following website: https://ir.tesla.com/</span>&#8203;<span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">contact-us#contact-us. Such shareholders who desire to contact our non-employee directors by mail may do so by writing to Tesla, Inc., 1 Tesla Road, Austin, Texas 78725, Attention: Legal Department. Our General Counsel, or someone acting in his or her place or his or her designee, receives these communications unfiltered by Tesla, forwards communications to the appropriate committee of the Board or non-employee director, and facilitates an appropriate response. Please note that requests for investor relations materials should be sent to ir@tesla.com.</span></div>

          <div style="margin-top:11.9pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Overview and Fiscal Year 2025 Company Highlights</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Our current executive compensation program, which was developed and approved by the Compensation Committee, generally consists of base salary and equity-based incentives, as well as other benefits generally available to employees. We combine these elements in order to formulate compensation packages with the goal of providing, on a total basis, competitive pay and aligning the interests of our NEOs with long-term shareholder interests by tying the value of their compensation to our long-term stock price and/or the achievement of financial, operational and strategic objectives. In 2025, Tesla&#8217;s full-year accomplishments under our executive leadership included the following:</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Model Y&#8217;s position as the best-selling vehicle of any kind globally for the full year 2025;</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Completion of the refresh of our vehicle lineup with the launch of the new Model Y;</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Deployment of 46.7 gigawatt-hours of energy storage, representing a 48.7% increase compared to the prior year; and</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Further progress in our transition from a hardware-centric business to a physical SI company, including through advancements in FSD (Supervised), the launch of our Robotaxi service, refinement of our production-primed Optimus bot design and expansion of our SI training infrastructure.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">For more information on how our portfolio of products helped transition the world to sustainable energy in 2025, a key component of our mission of amazing abundance, please refer to the Environment section of our 2025 Impact Report.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Compensation Philosophy</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Our mission is building a world of amazing abundance. This is a long-term mission, and our compensation programs reflect this&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;and our startup origins&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;in that they consist primarily of salary or wages and equity awards. Whereas salary or wages are intended to meet our employees&#8217; near-term liquidity needs, we believe that equity awards are an effective tool for retaining employees long-term and incentivizing performance, as they vest incrementally over a period of time or upon the achievement of specified performance milestones designed to be achieved over the medium and long term. During periods in which our stock price and the underlying value of </span>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">equity awards increase, their retention impact is even greater. We believe that the potential for such increases also creates an ownership culture that promotes holding equity, which in turn aligns the interests of our employees with the long-term interests of our shareholders. This compensation philosophy also allows our employees to grow their skill sets and contributions consistent with our long-term mission. For these reasons, our goal is to provide employees with the opportunity to participate in our equity programs, with certain cash-based bonus programs serving generally to accommodate specific incentive structures or liquidity needs. For more information on the impact equity ownership has had on our employees, please refer to the People and Community of our 2025 Impact Report.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In light of these considerations, we generally do not make annual grants of equity awards to our senior executives, including our NEOs, and instead grant equity awards from time to time based upon individual roles and contributions and the retentive impact of currently outstanding equity awards. By combining salary or wages with our equity award program, we strive to offer a total level of compensation that is competitive for specific roles within particular geographical markets.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In particular, we believe that compensation for the individuals who are responsible for Tesla&#8217;s strategic direction and operations (including those below the executive level as discussed below) should motivate them to achieve sustainable shareholder value and/or tangible milestones rather than to simply remain at Tesla or maintain the status quo.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">When grants are made to executive officers (other than our Chief Executive Officer), those grants generally comprise stock option awards, which have no intrinsic value at grant and accumulate value, if at all, only to the extent that our stock price increases following their grant and such stock options are exercised. Prior to 2025, grants to our Chief Executive Officer were in the form of stock options. Equity awards granted to our Chief Executive Officer in 2025 are discussed in &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below. In addition, because equity awards comprise a greater proportion of our executive officers&#8217; total level of compensation compared to comparable roles at peer companies, a sustained decrease in our stock price or failure to achieve the applicable operational milestones may result in a level of total compensation that is significantly less than that of such peer roles. Likewise, our outside director compensation program has been comprised primarily of equity awards that are entirely in the form of stock option awards, as well as relatively modest cash retainer payments that may be waived at the election of each director. Each director determined to forgo all equity and cash retainer payments for 2025, as they have done since 2021.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Performance Equity Awards</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">As discussed, we are committed to a pay for performance culture where we believe that key employees, whether at the Chief Executive Officer level, executive level or below the executive level, should be incentivized to drive sustainable shareholder value through the achievement of tangible operational milestones that meaningfully advance Tesla&#8217;s business.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:30pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Performance Equity Awards to Executives with Operational Goals</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-left:30pt; margin-top:6pt; width:457pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In 2012, we proposed the first CEO Performance Award, which aligned compensation incentives with measurable company performance tied to our core company goals. We continued that approach in 2018 and again in 2025 where we established ambitious milestones that only reward the recipient when the Company achieves both market capitalization and operational goals. Shareholders were rewarded with extraordinary performance when those goals were not only accomplished, but in a timeframe sooner than required. Other executives apart from our Chief Executive Officer have also been incentivized through equity awards tied to the achievement of certain operational goals.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style=" float:left; margin-left:20pt; line-height:12pt; margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>

            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Performance Equity Awards to Non-Executives with Operational Goals</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-left:30pt; margin-top:6pt; width:457pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In keeping with this pay for performance philosophy, while we offer to our general employee population time-vesting equity awards, we also grant from time to time equity awards to non-executive key employees that are earned solely based on the achievement of specified operational milestones. These operational milestones are designed as meaningful indicators </span>

            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Equity Awards to Other Employees</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

          <div style="margin-left:30pt; margin-top:6pt; width:457pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">For our broader employee population, we have also introduced programs which included, among others, awards which vested based on the Company achieving certain financial milestones, and award multipliers for hourly employees tied to Company vehicle deliveries and energy deployments. In this way, our compensation programs are designed to pay for performance at every level of the Company.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We evaluate our compensation philosophy and programs regularly and evolve them as circumstances merit with oversight by the Compensation Committee (and, as appropriate, a special committee of the Board of Directors), particularly with respect to executive and director compensation. For example, if our stock price experiences significant movement over a short period of time that results in a persistent change to equity compensation, certain adjustments may be considered to align our compensation programs to their intended purposes.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Key Factors in Determining Executive Compensation</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Role of Compensation Committee in 2025 Executive Compensation</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Compensation Committee has overall responsibility for reviewing and determining the compensation of our other executive officers. Members of the Compensation Committee are appointed by the Board. Currently, the Compensation Committee consists of three members of the Board: Ira Ehrenpreis (Chair), Robyn Denholm and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, none of whom is an executive officer of Tesla, and each of whom qualifies as an &#8220;independent director&#8221; under the Nasdaq rules and is deemed independent under all applicable requirements of the Securities and Exchange Commission and Tesla&#8217;s Corporate Governance Guidelines, which follow the Nasdaq framework for the determination of independence.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In 2025, the Board determined that it was in the best interests of Tesla to form a special committee, consisting of Ms.&#160;Denholm and Ms.&#160;Wilson-Thompson in their capacity as disinterested directors (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Special Committee</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), to consider, evaluate and determine whether it would be in the best interests of Tesla to retain and incentivize Mr.&#160;Musk, and if so, any methods, approaches or manners (including any new compensation plans or awards) for doing so consistent with all applicable legal and other requirements.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Role of Compensation Consultants for 2025 Executive Compensation</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Compensation Committee has the authority to engage, and has from time to time engaged, the services of outside consultants to assist in making decisions regarding the establishment of Tesla&#8217;s compensation philosophy and programs, including for executives and directors. In addition, in 2025, Compensia, Inc., a national consulting firm (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Compensia</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), was retained as a compensation consultant to advise the Special Committee with respect to the performance-based restricted stock award granted to Elon Musk in September&#160;2025 (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">2025 CEO Performance Award</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;).</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

        <div style="margin-top:23.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Role of Executive Officers in Compensation Decisions in 2025</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Historically, for executive officers other than our Chief Executive Officer, the Compensation Committee has sought and considered input from our Chief Executive Officer regarding such executive officers&#8217; responsibilities, performance and compensation. Specifically, our Chief Executive Officer recommends base salary increases and equity award levels for our senior personnel, and advises the Compensation Committee regarding the compensation program&#8217;s ability to attract, retain and motivate executive talent. These recommendations reflect compensation levels that our Chief Executive Officer believes are qualitatively commensurate with an executive officer&#8217;s individual qualifications, experience, responsibility level, functional role, knowledge, skills and individual performance, as well as Tesla&#8217;s performance. The Compensation Committee considers our Chief Executive Officer&#8217;s recommendations, but ultimately determines compensation in its judgment and approves the compensation for all of our executive officers (other than for our Chief Executive Officer, the compensation for whom in 2025 was recommended by the Special Committee to, and ultimately approved by, the Board and our shareholders).</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Compensation Committee meets regularly in executive session. Our Chief Executive Officer is not present during Compensation Committee deliberations or votes on his compensation and also recuses himself from sessions of the Board where the Board acts on the Compensation Committee&#8217;s recommendations regarding his compensation. In addition, the Board has established a management committee under the A&amp;R 2019 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Equity Award Committee</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) to grant and administer equity awards, subject to certain limitations, such as, among other things, maximum limits on the seniority of personnel to whom the Equity Award Committee may grant awards and the value of any individual award. For example, the Equity Award Committee is not authorized to grant awards to employees at or above the level of vice president. Moreover, pursuant to applicable law, the Equity Award Committee may not grant awards to its members, and the number of shares of our common stock underlying awards granted by it may not exceed amounts determined by the Board from time to time. The Board has delegated to the Compensation Committee oversight authority over the Equity Award Committee.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Role of Shareholder Say-on-Pay Votes</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">At our 2025 Annual Meeting, our shareholders approved the compensation of our NEOs, with approximately 78.2% of our shareholders present or represented by proxy and entitled to vote on the proposal at the meeting voting in favor of our compensation policies for our NEOs. Given these results, the Compensation Committee has decided to retain our overall approach to executive compensation while continuing to evaluate our practices.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">At the 2023 Annual Meeting, our shareholders indicated a preference for an annual shareholder advisory vote on the compensation of our NEOs. Consistent with the results of the shareholder vote, we intend to hold a shareholder advisory vote on executive compensation every year until the next vote on the frequency of shareholder advisory votes on executive compensation. We are required to hold a &#8220;say on frequency&#8221; vote at least every six&#160;years regarding how often to hold a shareholder advisory vote on the compensation of our NEOs.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Clawback Policy</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We maintain a clawback policy for compliance with Nasdaq listing standards and Section&#160;10D of the Exchange Act. This clawback policy applies to current and former executive officers in the event that the Company is required to prepare an accounting restatement due to the material noncompliance of the Company with any financial reporting requirement under securities laws; misconduct on the part of the executive is not required to trigger the clawback policy&#8217;s application. Under this clawback policy, we are required to recoup incentive-based compensation (as that term is defined in Section&#160;10D of the Exchange Act) erroneously received within the three completed fiscal&#160;years immediately preceding the date on which we are required to prepare an accounting restatement. Our Compensation Committee is responsible for overseeing the administration of this clawback policy.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">2025 Equity-Based Incentives</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Our equity award program is the primary vehicle for offering long-term incentives to our NEOs. The equity awards we have historically granted and currently grant to individuals other than our Chief Executive Officer are options to purchase shares of our common stock and restricted stock unit awards that are settled in shares of our common stock upon vesting. We have granted to our NEOs both awards that vest over a long-term period and awards that vest only upon the achievement of specified Tesla performance milestones, in each case subject to continued service. We emphasize the grant of stock option awards for our NEOs, which have value only to the extent, if any, that our stock price increases following their grant. Accordingly, since 2020, equity awards granted to our NEOs (other than our Chief Executive Officer) have primarily been in the form of stock options: Mr.&#160;Zhu, our Senior Vice President, APAC and Global Vehicle Manufacturing, received 100% of his equity award as stock options upon his promotion to Senior Vice President in 2023, and Mr.&#160;Taneja, our Chief Financial Officer, received approximately 80% of his equity award as stock options in 2024. As a result, a significant portion of our NEOs&#8217; total compensation is entirely at risk, depending on long-term stock price performance. Prior to 2025, grants to our Chief Executive Officer were in the form of stock option awards. Equity awards granted to our Chief Executive Officer in 2025 are discussed in &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>

To determine the form and amount of equity awards previously granted to NEOs, the Compensation Committee considers, among other things, the role and responsibility of the NEO, competitive market factors, equity awards previously granted to the NEO, the impact of any dramatic changes in our stock price over a short </span>

We do not have, nor do we plan to establish, any program, plan or practice to time equity award grants in coordination with releasing material non-public information, and the <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="ecd:AwardTmgHowMnpiCnsdrdTextBlock" id="ixv-13358"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" format="ixt:fixed-false" name="ecd:AwardTmgMnpiCnsdrdFlag" id="ixv-13359">Compensation Committee does not take material non-public information</ix:nonNumeric> into account when <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" format="ixt:fixed-true" name="ecd:AwardTmgPredtrmndFlag" id="ixv-13360">determining the timing and terms of equity awards</ix:nonNumeric>.</ix:nonNumeric> Tesla has <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" format="ixt:fixed-false" name="ecd:MnpiDiscTimedForCompValFlag" id="ixv-13361">not timed</ix:nonNumeric> the disclosure of material non-public information to affect the value of executive compensation.           <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We do not currently have, or plan to enter into, any specific arrangements with our NEOs providing for cash-based bonus awards, and historically we have rarely entered into such arrangements.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Non-Equity Incentive Plan&#160;Compensation</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We did not provide any non-equity incentive plan compensation to any of our NEOs in 2025, and we do not currently have, or plan to enter into, any specific arrangements with our NEOs providing for non-equity incentive plan compensation.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Perquisites</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Generally, we do not provide any perquisites or other personal benefits to our NEOs which are not offered on a non-discriminatory basis to all employees as well.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Health and Welfare Benefits</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Chief Executive Officer Compensation</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Overview</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Historically, in developing compensation recommendations for our Chief Executive Officer, the Compensation Committee and Special Committee, as applicable, have sought both to appropriately reward our Chief Executive Officer&#8217;s previous and current contributions and to create incentives for our Chief Executive Officer to continue to contribute significantly to successful results in the future. Each of the 2025 CEO Performance Award, the 2018 CEO Performance Award and the performance-based stock option award granted to our Chief Executive Officer in August&#160;2012 (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">2012 CEO Performance Award</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) incentivized future performance when granted. The grant of restricted stock to Mr.&#160;Musk in August&#160;2025 (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">2025 CEO Interim Award</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) was intended to retain him in recognition of his inability to exercise the fully earned 2018 CEO Performance Award due to the ongoing litigation then pending before the Delaware Supreme Court (together with its constituent and related litigation, &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tornetta</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;). Following the Delaware Supreme Court&#8217;s reinstatement of the 2018 CEO Performance Award, the 2025 CEO Interim Award was forfeited in its entirety in April&#160;2026, as discussed in &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation For Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201; Chief Executive Officer Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Equity Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 CEO Interim Award</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In addition to serving as our Chief Executive Officer since October&#160;2008, Mr.&#160;Musk has contributed significantly and actively to us since our earliest days in April&#160;2004 by recruiting executives and engineers, contributing to our position as a multi-sector innovator in SI, robotics, vehicle engineering and design, raising capital for us, bringing investors to us and raising our public awareness.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Cash Compensation</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Mr.&#160;Musk historically earned a base salary that reflected the applicable minimum wage requirements under California law, and he was subject to income taxes based on such base salary. However, he has never accepted his salary. Commencing in May&#160;2019 at Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s request, we eliminated altogether the earning and accrual of this base salary.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Equity Compensation</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">2025 CEO Interim Award</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Special Committee recognized the lack of meaningful compensation for Mr.&#160;Musk since the 2012 CEO Performance Award was last earned in 2017 as well as the continued uncertainty around a resolution in Tornetta and its impact on Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s ability to exercise the 2018 CEO Performance Award, and the Special Committee assessed the possibility of a good-faith payment in recognition of his accomplishments and to honor Tesla&#8217;s compensation promises. The Special Committee designed the 2025 CEO Interim Award to allow Tesla to immediately deliver the voting influence that Mr.&#160;Musk had stated that he desired, while requiring Mr.&#160;Musk to remain in a leadership role at Tesla over a two-year vesting period in order to maintain both the voting influence and the economics associated with the 2025 CEO Interim Award. The Special Committee ultimately determined that </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:-12pt;margin-bottom:25.71pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:9pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:7pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.35pt;">42</span><span style="font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.42pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;2026 Proxy Statement</span>

        <a href="#TOC" style="color:#003366;">Table of Contents</a>
      </div>
      <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;background-color:white;overflow:hidden;margin:2pt 0 17.5pt 0;position:relative;box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:23.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="margin-top:17pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">retaining and incentivizing Mr.&#160;Musk was of paramount importance to Tesla&#8217;s future and recommended that the Board of Directors approve the 2025 CEO Interim Award. On August&#160;3, 2025, the Board of Directors approved an award of 96,000,000 shares of restricted stock to Mr.&#160;Musk under the Company&#8217;s A&amp;R 2019 Equity Incentive Plan.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The 2025 CEO Interim Award was scheduled to vest upon the second anniversary of August&#160;3, 2025, subject to Mr.&#160;Musk remaining in continuous service as CEO or as an executive officer responsible for product development or operations (as approved by the Board&#8217;s disinterested directors) through such second anniversary. The 2025 CEO Interim Award also would have vested on an accelerated basis if Mr.&#160;Musk was serving either as our CEO or as an executive officer responsible for product development or operations upon a change in control or his death. However, the 2025 CEO Interim Award would be immediately forfeited and returned to the Company if, prior to vesting, there was a final, non-appealable judgment, order or decision of the Delaware courts with respect to the action captioned </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tornetta v. Elon Musk et al.,</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> C.A. No. 2018-0408-KSJM (Del. Ch.), or any pending or future appeal, including </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In re Tesla, Inc. Derivative Litigation,</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> Nos. 10, 2025, 11, 2025 (Del.) (a &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tornetta Decision Event</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) that resulted in Mr.&#160;Musk becoming able to exercise in full the 2018 CEO Performance Award.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Following the Delaware Supreme Court&#8217;s reinstatement of the 2018 CEO Performance Award on December&#160;19, 2025, reversing the Delaware Court of Chancery (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Court of Chancery</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) decision purporting to rescind the 2018 CEO Performance Award and the Court of Chancery&#8217;s final order on March&#160;18, 2026 implementing such reversal, on April&#160;21, 2026, the disinterested directors of the Board (with Mr.&#160;Musk and Mr.&#160;Kimbal Musk recused), acting as administrator of the 2025 CEO Interim Award, approved the determination that the final order and judgment allowing Mr.&#160;Musk to exercise the 2018 CEO Performance Award in full constituted a Tornetta Decision Event, resulting in the forfeiture of the 2025 CEO Interim Award by Mr.&#160;Musk on April&#160;21, 2026.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">2025 CEO Performance Award</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Following Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s successful achievement of the 2018 CEO Performance Award, the Special Committee recognized that Tesla lacked a go-forward incentive for Mr.&#160;Musk to motivate him to focus on pursuing the Company&#8217;s long-term potential in line with the vision described in Master Plan&#160;Part&#160;IV. Building upon the successful framework of the 2018 CEO Performance Award, the Special Committee designed the 2025 CEO Performance Award to motivate Mr.&#160;Musk to lead Tesla through its next phase of transformational growth, as described in Master Plan&#160;Part&#160;IV. On September&#160;3, 2025 (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">2025 CEO Performance Award Grant Date</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), the Board of Directors granted the 2025 CEO Performance Award, consisting of approximately 423.7 million shares of performance-based restricted stock to Mr.&#160;Musk, which was approved on November&#160;6, 2025 by our shareholders.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The 2025 CEO Performance Award is designed to retain and incentivize Mr.&#160;Musk by giving him the voting rights associated with the restricted common stock underlying the award as soon as such shares are earned but then requiring that Mr.&#160;Musk remain in service to vest in the economic benefits of the earned restricted common stock. Until such time as there are no shares under the 2025 CEO Performance Award that are not earned (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Unearned Shares</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s Unearned Shares will vote proportionately to the votes of all other shares of our capital stock that are present and entitled to vote at any annual or special meeting (or similar action) of our shareholders (including Mr.&#160;Musk).</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Generally, each of the 12 tranches of the 2025 CEO Performance Award will become &#8220;Earned Shares&#8221; upon Mr.&#160;Musk remaining in Eligible Service (as defined below) and the certification by disinterested directors that the following have been achieved: (i)&#160;the market capitalization milestone for such tranche and (ii)&#160;any one of the four operational milestones focused on strategic product goals (subject to deemed achievement for certain strategic product goals) or eight operational milestones focused on Adjusted EBITDA (clauses (i)&#160;and (ii), together the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Performance Milestones</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;). Mr.&#160;Musk will be able to direct the vote of such Earned Shares.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:10pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;font-size:8pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">(1)</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" line-height:10pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;font-size:8pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">Adjusted EBITDA is defined in the Tesla, Inc. 2025 CEO Performance Award Agreement, dated as of September&#160;3, 2025 (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.48pt;">2025 CEO Performance Award Agreement</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">&#8221;), as net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders before interest expense, provision (benefit) for income taxes, depreciation, amortization and impairment, stock-based compensation and digital assets gains and losses as reported in our financial statements on Forms 10-Q and 10-K (or other Exchange Act filings) filed with the SEC for the four consecutive fiscal quarters that immediately precede such determination date.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.16pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:10pt; margin-top:4.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:20pt;white-space:nowrap;font-size:8pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">(2)</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:4.1pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:10pt; text-align:left; margin-left:20pt;font-size:8pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">Meeting the last three Adjusted EBITDA operational milestones requires achieving Adjusted EBITDA of $400&#160;billion in three non-overlapping periods, each made up of four consecutive quarters.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.16pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The vesting date for each tranche of shares depends on when such shares become Earned Shares, which is based on the achievement of Performance Milestones. Generally, shares earned prior to the 5th anniversary of the 2025 CEO Performance Award Grant Date vest on the 7.5th anniversary, and shares that are earned after the 5th anniversary of the 2025 CEO Performance Award Grant Date vest on the 10th anniversary (each such 7.5-year and 10-year period, a &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Post-Milestone Service Period</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;); in each case, Mr.&#160;Musk must maintain continued employment either as our CEO or as an executive officer responsible for product development or operations through the applicable Post-Milestone Service Period (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Eligible Service</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;). Upon vesting, the vested shares will be reduced by an offset amount of $334.09 per share, unless Mr.&#160;Musk elects to pay such amounts in cash.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Shares in any tranche for which the Performance Milestones have not been achieved during the performance period will be forfeited automatically on the 10th anniversary of the 2025 CEO Performance Award Grant Date. Any unvested shares will be forfeited upon cessation of Eligible Service, except where Eligible Service is terminated without cause or due to death or disability, in which case Earned Shares will immediately vest. In a change in control of the Company, Unearned Shares may become Earned Shares based solely on market capitalization milestones as set out in the 2025 CEO Performance Award Agreement. Earned Shares will vest upon the change in control, and Unearned Shares will be automatically forfeited.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Mr.&#160;Musk must hold shares for five&#160;years after they become Earned Shares (regardless of whether such Earned Shares vest), subject to exceptions on or after vesting for (i)&#160;a change in control, (ii)&#160;satisfying taxes due in respect of vesting or (iii)&#160;transfers for estate planning purposes that involve a mere change of form or as may be permitted by our disinterested directors in their discretion consistent with our internal policies.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Historical Equity Compensation</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Prior to the stock option awards granted in December&#160;2009, Mr.&#160;Musk did not receive any equity compensation for his services for a period of five&#160;years.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In 2010 and 2011, Mr.&#160;Musk did not receive any equity grants, because the Compensation Committee believed his grants made in December&#160;2009 already provided sufficient motivation for Mr.&#160;Musk to perform his duties as Chief Executive Officer.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In August&#160;2012, to create incentives for continued long-term success from the then-recently launched Model S program as well as from Tesla&#8217;s then-planned Model X and Model 3 programs, and to further align executive compensation with increases in shareholder value, the Board granted to Mr.&#160;Musk the 2012 CEO Performance Award, comprised of a stock option award to purchase 79,123,515 shares (as adjusted for the 2020 Stock Split and 2022 Stock Split) of Tesla&#8217;s common stock, representing 5% of Tesla&#8217;s total issued and outstanding shares at the time of grant. The 2012 CEO Performance Award consisted of 10 equal vesting tranches, each requiring that Tesla meet a combination of (i)&#160;the achievement of a specified operational milestone relating to development of Model X or Model 3, aggregate vehicle production or a gross margin target and (ii)&#160;a sustained incremental $4&#160;billion increase in Tesla&#8217;s market capitalization from $3.2&#160;billion, Tesla&#8217;s market capitalization at the time of grant. Prior to the expiration of the 2012 CEO Performance Award in 2022, the market capitalization conditions for all of the 10 vesting tranches and nine of the 10 operational milestones had been achieved, and nine of the 10 tranches had vested.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Prior to 2018, the only additional equity awards received by Mr.&#160;Musk related to certain immaterial awards granted during 2013 pursuant to a patent incentive program that was available to our employees generally.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
