      <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;background-color:white;overflow:hidden;margin:2pt 0 17.5pt 0;position:relative;box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:23.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="margin-top:17pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">2018 CEO Performance Award</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In January&#160;2018, the Board of Directors granted a 10-year maximum term stock option to purchase 303,960,630 shares (as adjusted for the 2020 Stock Split and 2022 Stock Split) of Tesla&#8217;s common stock. The 2018 CEO Performance Award was divided equally among 12 separate tranches that were each equivalent to 1% of the issued and outstanding shares of Tesla&#8217;s common stock at the time of grant. Each of the 12 tranches of the 2018 CEO Performance Award vested upon certification by the Board that both (i)&#160;the market capitalization milestone for such tranche, which began at $100&#160;billion for the first tranche and increased by increments of $50&#160;billion thereafter, and (ii)&#160;the achievement of specified operational milestones relating to profitability, were met. All of the milestones were achieved in the lifetime of the award.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">On April&#160;21, 2026, the Board approved the Company&#8217;s entry into an agreement with Mr.&#160;Musk (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Implementation Agreement</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) implementing a process for Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s exercise of the 2018 CEO Performance Award.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The Implementation Agreement focuses on retaining Mr. Musk&#8217;s continued services by imposing a service-based vesting condition on the restricted shares of common stock issued to Mr.&#160;Musk upon exercise of the 2018 CEO Performance Award, requiring him to remain in continuous service as CEO or as an executive officer responsible for product development or operations (as approved by the Board&#8217;s disinterested directors) through January&#160;19, 2028 and commences the 2018 CEO Performance Award&#8217;s five-year holding period on the vesting date (rather than upon exercise of such award). The restricted shares will vest on an accelerated basis if Mr.&#160;Musk is serving either as our CEO or as an executive officer responsible for product development or operations upon a change in control, or upon his death, disability or termination without cause. The Implementation Agreement also provided that Mr.&#160;Musk could satisfy the exercise price of the 2018 CEO Performance Award by electing net settlement by the Company or paying cash and provides for cooperation between the Company and Mr.&#160;Musk to create a mutually agreeable plan to address Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s satisfaction of applicable tax obligations.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">On June 16, 2026, Mr. Musk exercised all 303,960,630 options and elected to net-settle the exercise price, pursuant to which the Company withheld 17,531,857 shares. The remaining 286,428,773 restricted shares issued upon exercise are scheduled to vest on January 19, 2028, subject to Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s satisfaction of the service-based vesting condition discussed above.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Realized Compensation</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;">
            <span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">For purposes of the table set forth under the caption &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Summary Compensation Table</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below, we are required to report pursuant to applicable SEC rules any equity award grants to Mr.&#160;Musk at values determined as of their respective grant dates and which are driven by certain assumptions prescribed by Financial Accounting Standards Board Accounting Standards Codification Topic 718, &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Stock Compensation</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">ASC&#160;Topic 718</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;). Moreover, we are required to report in &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Pay Ratio Disclosure</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below (i)&#160;Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s annual total compensation, (ii)&#160;the median of the annual total compensation of all Tesla employees qualifying for this analysis, other than Mr.&#160;Musk, in each case calculated pursuant to the methodology used for the table under &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Summary Compensation Table</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; and (iii)&#160;the ratio of the former to the latter.</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In addition, we are required to report in &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Option Exercises and Stock Vested</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below an amount for the &#8220;value realized&#8221; upon (i)&#160;any exercise by Mr.&#160;Musk of a stock option, which is based on the difference between the market price of the underlying shares at the time of exercise and the exercise price of the stock option and (ii)&#160;any vesting of a restricted stock or restricted stock unit award, based on the market price of the award at the time of vesting. Such amount is required to be reported even if Mr.&#160;Musk does not actually receive any cash from such exercise or vesting, either because he does not also sell any shares or because he sells only a number of shares sufficient to cover the related tax liabilities resulting from the exercise or vesting.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">As a result, there may be a significant disconnect between what is reported as compensation for Mr.&#160;Musk in a given year in such sections and the value actually realized as compensation in that year or over a period of time. Moreover, the vast majority of compensation in respect of past equity award grants to Mr.&#160;Musk, including the 2012 CEO Performance Award, the 2018 CEO Performance Award and the 2025 CEO Performance Award, was structured to be incentives for </span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">future</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> performance with their value realizable only if Tesla&#8217;s stock price appreciated compared to the dates of the grants, and if the Company achieved applicable vesting requirements.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;font-style:italic;">
            <span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">To supplement the disclosures in &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Summary Compensation Table,</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Pay Ratio Disclosure</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; and &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Option Exercises and Stock Vested</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below, we have included the following table, which shows the total realized compensation of Mr.&#160;Musk for the last three fiscal&#160;years, as well as the ratio of Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s realized compensation to the median of the annual total compensation of all other Tesla employees qualifying for this analysis as reported under &#8220;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Pay Ratio Disclosure.</span><span style="font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; Realized compensation is not a substitute for reported compensation in evaluating our compensation structure, but we believe that realized compensation is an important factor in understanding that the value of compensation that Mr.&#160;Musk ultimately realizes is dependent on a number of additional factors, including: (i)&#160;the vesting of certain of his option awards only upon the successful achievement of a number of market capitalization increase and operational milestone targets; (ii)&#160;the fact that Mr.&#160;Musk does not receive any cash if he does not actually sell shares and thereby reduce his investment in us, and he does not receive any cash to the extent that he sells only shares sufficient to cover income taxes with respect to his awards (including stock options exercised solely to avoid their expiration in accordance with their terms); and (iii)&#160;the then-current market value of our common stock at the times at which Mr.&#160;Musk may elect to actually sell his shares.</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-bottom:63pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Tax and Accounting Considerations</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Sections&#160;280G and 409A</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">. We have not provided or committed to provide any executive officer or director with a gross-up or other reimbursement for tax amounts the executive might pay pursuant to Section&#160;280G or Section&#160;409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;). Section&#160;280G and related Code sections provide that executive officers, directors who hold significant shareholder interests and certain other service providers could be subject to significant additional excise taxes if they receive payments or benefits in connection with a change in control of Tesla that exceeds certain limits, and that we or our successor could lose a deduction on the amounts subject to the additional tax. Section&#160;409A also imposes additional significant taxes on the individual in the event that an executive officer, director or service provider of certain types receives &#8220;deferred compensation&#8221; that does not meet the requirements of Section&#160;409A.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tax Deduction Limit</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">. Section&#160;162(m) of the Code generally disallows a tax deduction to public corporations for compensation greater than $1,000,000 paid in any fiscal year to certain executive officers. The Compensation Committee has not adopted a formal policy regarding tax deductibility of compensation paid to our executive officers and reserves the right to pay compensation that may not be deductible to Tesla if it determines that doing so would be in the best interests of Tesla. </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Accounting Implications</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">. We follow ASC Topic 718 for our stock-based compensation awards. ASC Topic 718 requires companies to measure the compensation expense for all stock-based compensation awards made to employees and directors based on the grant date &#8220;fair value&#8221; of these awards. This calculation is performed for accounting purposes and reported in the compensation tables below, even though our NEOs may never realize any value from their awards. ASC Topic 718 also requires companies to recognize the compensation cost of their stock-based compensation awards in their income statements over the period that an executive officer is required to render service in exchange for the option or other award.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Other Information</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">On June&#160;4, 2018, a Tesla shareholder filed a shareholder derivative complaint in the Court of Chancery against Mr.&#160;Musk and certain current and former Tesla directors in connection with the Board&#8217;s approval of the 2018 CEO Performance Award. On January&#160;30, 2024, the Court of Chancery issued a post-trial opinion that granted the plaintiff&#8217;s request that the 2018 CEO Performance Award be fully rescinded. In addition, following the recommendation of a special committee of the Board, the Board (with Messrs. Elon Musk and Kimbal Musk recusing themselves) determined that the ratification of the 2018 CEO Performance Award was in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders, approved the ratification (the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Ratification</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;) of the 2018 CEO Performance Award, directed that the Ratification be submitted to the shareholders at the 2024 annual meeting, and recommended that shareholders approve the Ratification. The Ratification was approved by the shareholders at the 2024 annual meeting. Following the Ratification, the director defendants, joined by Tesla, requested that the Court of Chancery revise its decision to rescind the 2018 CEO Performance Award. On December&#160;2, 2024, the Court of Chancery rejected the request to revise its decision and awarded plaintiff&#8217;s counsel fees in the amount of $345&#160;million. A final judgment was entered by the Court of Chancery, and the director defendants and Tesla appealed the decisions to the Delaware Supreme Court. On December&#160;19, 2025, the Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Court of Chancery&#8217;s judgment. The Supreme Court held that the rescission of the 2018 CEO Performance Award was improper, awarded Tesla nominal damages of $1, and reduced the attorneys&#8217; fee award. On January&#160;6, 2026, the Supreme Court issued its mandate to the Court of Chancery, and on March&#160;18, 2026, the Court of Chancery entered its Amended Final Order and Judgment, awarding Tesla $1 in nominal damages and plaintiff&#8217;s counsel approximately $65&#160;million inclusive of all fees, costs and post-trial interest. </span>
          </div>
        </div>

The beginning of the measurement period is December&#160;31, 2020. The Company has never declared or paid cash dividends on its common stock. The dollar amounts reported in the table are the value of an initial $100 investment made on December 31, 2020, equal to $100 multiplied by one plus the TSR percentage calculated as described above.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.16pt;"> </span>

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-bottom:220pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Description of Relationships Between Compensation Actually Paid and Performance</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Relationship Between Compensation Actually Paid to the CEO and Net Income, Revenue and TSR</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In 2025, compensation actually paid to the CEO was $10.37 billion, an increase from $0 in 2024. Over this same period, TSR increased by 11.0%, net income decreased by 46.1% and revenue decreased by 2.9%.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">From 2023 to 2024, compensation actually paid to the CEO decreased by 100.0%. Over this same period, TSR increased by 62.3%, net income decreased by 52.2% and revenue increased by 0.9%.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">From 2022 to 2023, compensation actually paid to the CEO increased by 114.5%. Over this same period, TSR increased by 103.8%, net income increased by 19.0% and revenue increased by 18.8%.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">From 2021 to 2022, compensation actually paid to the CEO decreased by 164.6%. Over this same period, TSR decreased by 65.3%, net income increased by 123.0% and revenue increased by&#160;51.4%. </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">As of the end of the 2025 fiscal year, Mr.&#160;Musk does not earn a base salary. Mr. Musk received compensation in the form of equity under the 2025 CEO Interim Award and the 2025 CEO Performance Award. </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">See</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Equity Compensation</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; for more information. </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The earning and vesting of shares under Mr. Musk&#8217;s 2025 CEO Performance Award are tied to specific market capitalization and operational milestones focusing on product goals and adjusted EBITDA. The vesting of the 2025 CEO Interim Award was tied to Mr. Musk remaining in continuous service as CEO or as an executive officer responsible for product development or operations (as approved by the Board&#8217;s disinterested directors) through the second anniversary of August 3, 2025. However, the compensation actually paid as calculated pursuant to Item 402(v) of Regulation S-K is based on the accounting changes in the fair value of such restricted stock awards, which varies significantly with the performance of our common stock.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">As the 2025 CEO Performance Award is a performance-based award, only the tranche determined to be probable as of December 31, 2025 was included in Mr. Musk&#8217;s compensation actually paid in 2025. Following the Delaware Supreme Court&#8217;s reinstatement of the 2018 CEO Performance Award, the 2025 CEO Interim Award was forfeited in its entirety in April 2026 and was not included in the compensation actually paid to Mr. Musk.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Thus, because the Company TSR is calculated from the beginning of the earliest year presented, a positive TSR does not necessarily correlate to an increase in compensation actually paid if the increase in TSR is less significant relative to a prior year. While a positive TSR may not align with an increase in compensation actually paid, as further demonstrated by the following graph, any decreases in TSR would align with decreases in compensation actually paid. </span>
          </div>

          <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_CompActuallyPaidVsTotalShareholderRtnTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="ecd:CompActuallyPaidVsTotalShareholderRtnTextBlock" id="ixv-8674"><div style="position:relative;margin-top:6pt; text-align:center; width:487pt;">
            <img alt="[MISSING IMAGE: bc_tsr-pn.jpg]" src="bc_tsr-pn.jpg" style="height: 322px; width: 620px;"/>
          </div></ix:nonNumeric>
          <div style="margin-top:14.69pt; width:487pt; line-height:10.5pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Relationship Between Average Compensation Actually Paid to Non-CEO NEOs and Net Income, Revenue and TSR</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">From 2024 to 2025, compensation actually paid to the other NEOs decreased by 92.4%. Over this same period, TSR increased by 11.0%, net income decreased by 46.1% and revenue decreased by 2.9%.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">From 2023 to 2024, compensation actually paid to the other NEOs increased by 95.0%. Over this same period, TSR increased by 62.3%, net income decreased by 52.2% and revenue increased by 0.9%.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">From 2022 to 2023, compensation actually paid to the other NEOs increased by 127.7%. Over this same period, TSR increased by 103.8%, net income increased by 19.0%, and revenue increased by 18.8%.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">From 2021 to 2022, compensation actually paid to the other NEOs decreased by 122.5%. Over this same period, TSR decreased by 65.3%, net income increased by 123.0%, and revenue increased by 51.4%.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Though our other NEOs do receive a base salary, a significant portion of their compensation actually paid consists of equity awards. As the compensation actually paid as calculated pursuant to Item&#160;402(v) of Regulation&#160;S-K is based on the accounting changes in the fair value of such options and restricted stock units through their vesting dates, the value varies significantly with the performance of our common stock. Thus, because the Company TSR is calculated from the beginning of the earliest year presented, a positive overall TSR does not necessarily correlate to an increase in compensation actually paid if the stock price decreased in a given year.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">From 2022 to 2023, compensation actually paid to our other NEOs was impacted by Zachary Kirkhorn&#8217;s departure in December&#160;2023, which led to certain forfeitures of unvested awards. From 2023 to 2024, the amount of increase in compensation actually paid to other NEOs was affected by Andrew Baglino&#8217;s departure in April&#160;2024, which led to certain forfeitures of unvested awards.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">While a positive TSR may not align with an increase in compensation actually paid, as further demonstrated by the following graph, any decreases in TSR would align with decreases in compensation actually paid.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.27pt;">Potential Payments Upon Termination or Change in Control as of December&#160;31, 2025</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.3pt;"> </span>

          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In accordance with SEC rules, we do not have an employment agreement for any specific term with any of our named executive officers. Moreover, we do not have any contract, agreement, plan or arrangement that would result in payments to a named executive officer at, following, or in connection with any termination of employment, including resignation, severance, retirement or a constructive termination of employment of a named executive officer, or a change in control of Tesla or a change in the named executive officer&#8217;s responsibilities, other than the 2025 CEO Performance Award, and, prior to its forfeiture in its entirety in April&#160;2026, the 2025 CEO Interim Award, as described in &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Equity Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 CEO Performance Award&#8221;</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> and </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8220;Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Equity Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 CEO Interim Award</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; above, respectively. However, no portion of the 2025 CEO Performance Award would have vested if Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s service had terminated without cause or due to death or disability on December&#160;31, 2025 because none of the shares of performance-based restricted stock under the 2025 CEO Performance Award had become Earned Shares prior to such date, and the vesting of the 2025 CEO Performance Award based solely upon the achievement of market capitalization milestones as measured at the time of a change in control of Tesla, by its nature, cannot be estimated at this time. The 2025 CEO Interim Award would have vested upon the occurrence of a change in control or Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s death on December&#160;31, 2025, and such vesting would require his payment of a purchase price of $23.34 per share of restricted stock that vests. Using the closing price of our common stock on December&#160;31, 2025 ($449.72), the estimated value of such vesting of the 2025 CEO Interim Award, less the aggregate purchase price payable by Mr.&#160;Musk ($2,240,640,000), is $40,932,480,000. However, the 2025 CEO Interim Award was forfeited in its entirety in April&#160;2026. The Implementation Agreement, which includes provisions for vesting in connection with certain terminations of employment and change in control, was entered into after December&#160;31, 2025, as described in &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Chief Executive Officer Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;Historical Equity Compensation&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2018 CEO Performance Award</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">.&#8221;</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

        <div style="margin-top:23.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">capitalization and achievement of certain performance milestones. Because equity awards are generally made available to Tesla employees, this also means that Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s compensation is tied to the success of Tesla employees. In accordance with SEC rules, we are providing a ratio of (i)&#160;Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s 2025 annual total compensation to (ii)&#160;the median of the 2025 annual total compensation of all applicable qualifying Tesla employees other than Mr.&#160;Musk, in each case calculated pursuant to the disclosure requirements of &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Summary Compensation Table</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; above. As we continue our expansion, the median annual total compensation of our employees reflects differences in local compensation scales and practices. However, these amounts rely on assumptions and projections made pursuant to accounting rules and are not necessarily indicative of the actual value that was or may be realized. In particular, the vast majority of the 2025 annual total compensation for Mr.&#160;Musk reflects an accounting-driven valuation for the 2025 CEO Performance Award, as to which no shares have vested as of the date of this filing, and which, upon vesting, is further subject to an offset of a number of shares equal to $334.09 per vested share, unless Mr.&#160;Musk elects to pay such offset amount in cash. In addition, the 2025 annual total compensation includes the value of the 2025 CEO Interim Award of approximately $26.1&#160;billion, which was forfeited in its entirety in April&#160;2026.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Mr.&#160;Musk&#8217;s 2025 annual total compensation, as reported under &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Executive Compensation for Fiscal Year 2025&#8201;&#8212;&#8201;2025 Summary Compensation Table</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">,&#8221; was $158,359,009,867, the vast majority of which reflects an accounting-driven valuation for the 2025 CEO Performance Award, as explained above, and the median 2025 annual total compensation of all other qualifying employees, as determined pursuant to the methodology set forth below, was $62,786. Consequently, the applicable ratio of such amounts for 2025 was 2,522,203:1. However, using the Total CEO realized compensation for 2025, such ratio was 0.00:1.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Our methodology for identifying the median of the 2025 annual total compensation for each individual other than Mr.&#160;Musk was as follows:</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style=" float:left; line-height:12pt; margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:10pt;white-space:nowrap;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8226;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
          <div style=" margin-top:5.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt; text-align:left; margin-left:10pt;">
            <!--blacklining:none;-->
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We selected December&#160;31, 2025, which is within the last three&#160;months of 2025, as the date upon which we would identify the &#8220;median employee&#8221; because it enabled us to make such identification in a reasonably efficient and economical manner.</span><span style="color:#646469;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

Tesla&#8217;s management and the Compensation Committee have assessed the risks associated with Tesla&#8217;s compensation policies and practices for all employees, including non-executive officers. These include risks relating to setting ambitious targets for our employees&#8217; compensation or the vesting of their equity awards and our emphasis on at-risk equity-based compensation, and the potential impact of such practices on the retention or decision-making of our employees, particularly our senior management.             <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>

        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="margin-left:20pt; width:467pt; line-height:10pt;font-size:8pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">(the &#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.48pt;">Detroit Settlement Agreement</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">&#8221;) in connection with a derivative action brought by a purported Tesla shareholder regarding compensation awards granted to Tesla&#8217;s directors, other than Mr.&#160;Musk, between 2017 and 2020, the Board has permanently forgone the Board Stock Option Grants for 2021 and 2022, and the Board did not receive any compensation for Board service for 2021 and 2022. Ms.&#160;Denholm, Mr.&#160;Ehrenpreis, Mr.&#160;Kimbal Musk, Mr.&#160;Murdoch and Ms.&#160;Wilson-Thompson have also permanently forgone any compensation for Board service for 2023. </span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.48pt;">See</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;"> &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.48pt;">Other Information</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.48pt;">&#8221; below for additional information regarding the Detroit Settlement Agreement.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.16pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Non-Employee Director Compensation Arrangements</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Overview and Philosophy</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The compensation program for Tesla&#8217;s non-employee directors is designed to be consistent with our compensation philosophy for our employees, with an emphasis on equity-based compensation over cash in order to align the value of their compensation with the market value of our stock, and consequently, with the long-term interests of our shareholders. Moreover, while we offer to our general employee population restricted stock&#160;units that will retain some value even if the market value of our stock decreases, the equity-based compensation to our directors has been exclusively in the form of stock options, which have zero initial value and accumulate value, if at all, only to the extent that our stock price increases following their grant, through the applicable vesting dates and until such stock options are ultimately exercised and the underlying shares are sold. The remaining portion of our directors&#8217; compensation has consisted of cash retainer payments that are relatively modest compared to peer companies and that may be waived at the election of each director. Consequently, a large portion and, in some cases, the entirety, of each of our non-employee directors&#8217; compensation is entirely at risk, and fluctuating stock prices have at times resulted in 100% of the vested stock options then held by each of our non-employee directors being out-of-the-money.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In 2020 and 2021, the Compensation Committee reviewed the Director Compensation Policy with the aid of Compensia and in light of Tesla&#8217;s exceptional performance and commitment to at-risk director compensation in the form of annual stock option awards to ensure continued alignment of the interests of directors with those of Tesla&#8217;s shareholders. Following such review, the Compensation Committee recommended that the Board approve a resolution that all existing directors forgo any automatic grants of annual stock option awards under the Director Compensation Policy or otherwise previously approved by the Board until July&#160;2022 unless the Board earlier acts to amend the Director Compensation Policy or otherwise amends such resolution. In June&#160;2021, the Board unanimously approved and adopted this resolution and in May&#160;2022, the Board agreed to further forgo the Board Stock Option Grants until the Board earlier acts to amend the Director Compensation Policy or otherwise amends such resolution. The Compensation Committee intends to make further recommendations with respect to the Board&#8217;s compensation program for any directors who join the Board after the date of this resolution, as well as for future periods of service by existing directors, following further periodic reviews.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:8pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.5pt;">Other Information</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Historically, the terms of our non-employee director stock option awards provided that, if following a change in control of Tesla, the service of a non-employee director were terminated, all unvested stock options granted to the director would fully vest and become immediately exercisable. There are currently no unvested stock option awards held by non-employee directors.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Non-employee directors may also have their travel, lodging and related expenses associated with attending Board or Board committee meetings reimbursed by Tesla.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">On June&#160;17, 2020, a Tesla shareholder filed a shareholder derivative complaint in the Delaware Chancery Court, purportedly on behalf of Tesla, against certain of Tesla&#8217;s current and former directors regarding compensation awards granted to Tesla&#8217;s directors, other than Mr.&#160;Musk, between 2017 and 2020. The suit asserts claims for breach of fiduciary duty and unjust enrichment and seeks declaratory and injunctive relief, unspecified damages and other relief.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">On July 14, 2023, the parties filed the Detroit Settlement Agreement, which does not involve an admission of any wrongdoing by any party. In a January 13, 2025 final judgment, the Court of </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:-12pt;margin-bottom:25.71pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:9pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:7pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.35pt;">62</span><span style="font-weight:normal;letter-spacing:0.42pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;2026 Proxy Statement</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
        </div>
        <hr style="display:none"/>
      </div>
      <div style="padding:0pt;margin:0pt;font-family:calibri, arial, sans-serif;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size:9pt;line-height:9pt;width:595.31pt;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;">
        <a href="#TOC3" style="color:#003366;">Table of Contents</a><a id="tPOS">&#8203;</a>
      </div>
      <div style="page-break-after:always; width:595.3pt;background-color:white;overflow:hidden;margin:2pt 0 17.5pt 0;position:relative;box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">
        <div style="margin-top:23.85pt;height:24pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="margin-top:17pt; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>
            <br/>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:0.149999999999999pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Chancery approved the settlement, and over Tesla&#8217;s objection, awarded plaintiff&#8217;s counsel fees in the amount of approximately $176 million.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Tesla appealed the amount of the attorneys&#8217; fee award to the Delaware Supreme Court. On January&#160;30, 2026, the Delaware Supreme Court agreed with Tesla&#8217;s appeal and reduced the attorneys&#8217; fee award from $176&#160;million to $71&#160;million. The Supreme Court also affirmed the Court of Chancery&#8217;s approval of the Detroit Settlement Agreement.</span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In May&#160;2025, the Company implemented certain provisions of the Detroit Settlement Agreement by cancelling the options requiring cancellation under its terms.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:17pt;color:#646469;font-size:15pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.27pt;">Pledging of Shares</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.3pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">The ability of our directors and executive officers to pledge Tesla stock for personal loans and investments is inherently related to their compensation due to our use of equity awards and promotion of long-termism and an ownership culture. Moreover, providing these individuals flexibility in financial planning without having to rely on the sale of shares aligns their interests with those of our shareholders.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In order to mitigate the risk of forced sales of pledged shares, the Board has a policy that limits pledging of Tesla stock by our directors and executive officers. Pursuant to this policy, directors and executive officers may pledge their stock (exclusive of options, warrants, restricted stock&#160;units or other rights to purchase stock) as collateral for loans and investments, provided that the maximum aggregate loan or investment amount collateralized by such pledged stock does not exceed (i)&#160;with respect to our CEO, the lesser of $3.5&#160;billion and twenty-five&#160;percent (25%) of the total value of the pledged stock, or (ii)&#160;with respect to our directors and officers other than our CEO, fifteen&#160;percent (15%) of the total value of the pledged stock. Notwithstanding such limitations, to facilitate the orderly disposition of shares and avoid market disruption, the 2025 CEO Performance Award and the Implementation Agreement each provide that our CEO may pledge any shares of common stock that he beneficially owns (including, without limitation, shares awarded under the 2025 CEO Performance Award and the 2018 CEO Performance Award) for the purposes of satisfying the payment of taxes attributable to required tax withholding or any Offset Amount due in respect of the 2025 CEO Performance Award.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;font-style:italic;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Example: A director (other than our CEO) pledges 1,000 shares as collateral for a loan, and the current stock price is $800 per share. The director may borrow up to 15% of 1,000 x $800, or $120,000, against such shares. If the stock price later increases to $1,600 per share, the director may borrow up to an additional $120,000 against the pledged shares. If the director borrows the full allowable amount of $240,000 and the stock price then decreases to $1,200, the director must repay $60,000 to maintain compliance with the 15% limit under the pledging policy.</span><span style="font-style:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">See</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> &#8220;</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Ownership of Securities</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221; below for information regarding any shares pledged by our directors or executive officers as of September&#160;30, 2026; however, such pledging does </span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">not</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;"> indicate the extent to which there may be actual borrowings against such shares as of such date, which may be substantially less than the value of the shares pledged. As of December&#160;31, 2025, based on written representations of our directors and executive officers to the Company, the aggregate loan or investment amount collateralized by our directors and executive officers&#8217; pledged shares was less than 1% of the total value of the pledged shares.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">We require our directors and executive officers to make written representations, at least annually, that he or she is in compliance with our pledging policy. If a director or executive officer wishes to take a loan collateralized by pledged stock, Tesla management works with the director or executive officer during the original loan approval, and subsequently monitors compliance with this policy by regularly reviewing and requesting updates from the applicable director or executive officer on his or her pledged stock amount and loan amount. If necessary, Tesla management will report to the Board or its committees the extent to which any officer or director has pledged shares of Company stock. We believe that this monitoring is effective and includes appropriate controls, and we have confirmed that each of our directors and executive officers who has pledged stock is and has been compliant with this policy since our last confirmation. </span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="margin-top:29pt;min-height:12pt;margin-left:54pt;width:487pt;">
          <div style="text-align:center; width:487pt; line-height:12pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#160;</span>

            <span style="letter-spacing:0.8pt;">Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.32pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.55pt;">Review of Related Person Transactions</span><span style="font-weight:normal;font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.22pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In accordance with the charter for the Audit Committee of the Board and our written Policies and Procedures with Respect to Related Person Transactions (&#8220;</span><span style=" text-decoration:underline #000000 solid;letter-spacing:0.6pt;">RPT Policy</span><span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">&#8221;), our Audit Committee reviews and approves any related person transactions.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">For purposes of these procedures, &#8220;related person&#8221; and &#8220;transaction&#8221; have the meanings contained in Item&#160;404 of Regulation&#160;S-K.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Under the RPT Policy, the Audit Committee must review and approve all transactions in which (i)&#160;Tesla or one of its subsidiaries is a participant, (ii)&#160;the amount involved exceeds $120,000 and (iii)&#160;a related person has a direct or indirect material interest, other than transactions available to all Tesla employees generally.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">In assessing a related person transaction brought before it for approval, the Audit Committee considers, among other factors, whether the related person transaction is on terms no less favorable than terms generally available to an unaffiliated third party under the same or similar circumstances and the extent of the related person&#8217;s interest in the transaction. The Audit Committee may then approve or disapprove the transaction in its discretion, or may request additional information.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:6pt; width:487pt; line-height:11.5pt;">
            <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Related person transactions will be disclosed in the applicable SEC filing as required by the rules of the SEC.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:12pt; width:487pt; line-height:13pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">

In March&#160;2025, xAI and X effected a transaction under which xAI and X became wholly-owned subsidiaries of a new parent company named X.AI Holdings Corp. On February 2, 2026, xAI Holdings was acquired by and became a wholly owned subsidiary of SpaceX pursuant to a merger transaction.</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif ;letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </span>

In connection with the investment, Tesla and xAI also entered into a framework agreement that, among other things, builds upon the existing relationship between Tesla and xAI by providing a framework for evaluating potential collaborations, with any specific projects to be implemented through separate negotiations. As a result of the SpaceX and xAI Holdings merger, Tesla&#8217;s right to acquire shares of Series E Preferred Stock of xAI Holdings under the previously disclosed agreement with xAI Holdings was converted into the right to acquire shares of Class A common stock of SpaceX in accordance with the terms of the underlying merger agreement. Tesla completed its investment of approximately $2.00 billion to acquire shares of Class A common stock of SpaceX on March 12, 2026.</span>

                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">Our Audit Committee is composed of four directors: Robyn Denholm (Chair), Joe Gebbia, Jack Hartung and James Murdoch. The Audit Committee is comprised solely of directors who satisfy applicable independence and other requirements under Nasdaq listing standards and applicable securities laws. The Board has determined that each of Ms.&#160;Denholm and Mr.&#160;Hartung is an &#8220;audit committee financial expert&#8221; as defined in the rules of the SEC.</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.8pt; line-height:9pt;font-weight:bold;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.45pt;">Oversight</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:5.8pt; line-height:10.78pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">The Audit Committee assists the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities by:</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style=" float:left; line-height:10.78pt; margin-top:7.81pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:9pt;white-space:nowrap;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">&#8226;</span>
                      <br/>
                    </div>

                      <!--blacklining:none;-->
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">Providing oversight, recommendations, and under specified thresholds, approvals, regarding significant financial matters and investment practices, including any material acquisitions and divestitures;</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
                    <div style=" float:left; line-height:10.78pt; margin-top:7.81pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:9pt;white-space:nowrap;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">&#8226;</span>
                      <br/>
                    </div>
                    <div style=" margin-top:7.81pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:10.78pt; text-align:left; margin-left:9pt;">
                      <!--blacklining:none;-->
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">Monitoring the integrity of Tesla&#8217;s financial statements and Tesla&#8217;s compliance with legal and regulatory requirements as they relate to financial statements or accounting matters; and</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
                    <div style=" float:left; line-height:10.78pt; margin-top:7.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:left; width:9pt;white-space:nowrap;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">&#8226;</span>
                      <br/>
                    </div>
                    <div style=" margin-top:7.8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:10.78pt; text-align:left; margin-left:9pt;">
                      <!--blacklining:none;-->
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">Reviewing the adequacy and effectiveness of Tesla&#8217;s internal control policies and procedures in addition to Tesla&#8217;s risk management, data privacy, data security and SI. </span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="clear:both; padding:0pt; margin:0pt;font-size:0pt;line-height:0pt;">&#8203;</div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.8pt; line-height:10.78pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">In addition to overseeing key risks in the areas of data security and privacy, crisis risk management, ethics and compliance, and sustainability, as discussed below, the Audit Committee is also responsible for overseeing risks in other areas of our business and operations.</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.8pt; line-height:9pt;font-weight:bold;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.45pt;">Additional Key Objectives</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-left:9pt; margin-top:7.8pt; line-height:9pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">Data Security</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:5.8pt; line-height:10.78pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">The Audit Committee is responsible for reviewing the adequacy and effectiveness of Tesla&#8217;s policies and practices with respect to data security risk exposures, and providing oversight over Tesla&#8217;s data security policies and monitoring programs. The Audit Committee receives regular updates from senior management, including our Chief Information Officer, on data security risk reviews of Tesla&#8217;s key business segments and products, procedures to assess and address data security risk and the effectiveness of data security technologies and solutions deployed internally.</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-left:9pt; margin-top:7.8pt; line-height:9pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">Data Privacy</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.8pt; line-height:10.78pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.54pt;">Privacy is integral to our business and Tesla is committed to the protection of the personal data which it processes as part of its business and on behalf of customers. We have established a robust global privacy program with oversight by executive management, an independent Data Protection Officer for our European regulated entities, and, at the Board level, our Audit Committee. Our governance and accountability measures promote core principles of data privacy, while the collaborative effort between our Information Security Team and Legal Team enables us to meet our regulatory requirements and demonstrate compliance. For more information on our data privacy policies and principles, please refer to the Privacy, Security and AI section of our 2025 Impact Report.</span>
                    </div>

                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-left:9.25pt; line-height:11.1pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">Crisis Risk Management</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.86pt; line-height:11.08pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">In response to extraordinary events, the Audit Committee receives regular updates from senior management.</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-left:9.25pt; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:9.25pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">Ethics</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:11.09pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">The Audit Committee has oversight of Tesla&#8217;s compliance with legal, regulatory and ethical compliance programs. The Audit Committee has established procedures for the receipt, retention and treatment of complaints about accounting, internal controls over financial reporting or audit matters, and procedures for the confidential, anonymous submission by employees of concerns regarding questionable accounting or audit matters. We encourage employees and third parties to report concerns about our internal controls over financial reporting, auditing matters or any other ethical wrongdoing. To report such a concern, please visit https://digitalassets.tesla.com/tesla-contents/image/upload/</span>&#8203;<span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">Business_Code_Of_Ethics where you will find various reporting options.</span></div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-left:9.25pt; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:9.25pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">Sustainability</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:11.08pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">The Audit Committee is responsible for reviewing and discussing the assessment of the Company&#8217;s annual Impact Report, and, as deemed appropriate, other sustainability-related disclosures.</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-left:9.25pt; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:9.25pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">Selection &amp; Oversight of External Auditor</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:11.09pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">The Audit Committee appoints, compensates, oversees and manages Tesla&#8217;s relationship with its independent registered public accounting firm, which reports directly to the Audit Committee. In selecting PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the Company&#8217;s independent registered public accounting firm, the Audit Committee annually evaluates the firm&#8217;s qualifications and performance; the quality and candor of its communications with the Audit Committee and the Company; independence and integrity; efficiency and the appropriateness of fees; benefits of audit firm or lead partner rotations; and the comprehensiveness of evaluations of internal controls. The Audit Committee also considers the relative costs, benefits, challenges and other potential impacts of selecting a different independent public accounting firm.</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:11.09pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">In reviewing and approving audit and non-audit service fees, the Audit Committee considers a number of factors, including the scope and quality of work, as well as an assessment of the impact on auditor independence of non-audit fees and services. During the course of the fiscal year, the Audit Committee is given regular updates regarding audit-related and non-audit-related fees.</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:9.25pt;font-weight:bold;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.462pt;">Audit Committee Report</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="white-space:normal; margin-top:7.85pt; line-height:11.09pt;">
                      <span style="letter-spacing:0.555pt;">The Audit Committee assists the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities for oversight of the integrity of Tesla&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, our internal controls over financial reporting, our compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, the organization and performance of our internal audit function and the qualifications, independence and performance of our independent registered public accounting firm.</span>
                    </div>

                <div style="line-height:11.5pt;">
                  <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">An organization that holds shares of Tesla&#8217;s common stock for a beneficial owner will have the discretion to vote on routine proposals if it has not received voting instructions from the beneficial owner at least ten days prior to the 2026 Annual Meeting. A broker &#8220;non-vote&#8221; occurs when a broker, bank or other intermediary that is otherwise counted as present or represented by proxy does not receive voting instructions from the beneficial owner and does not have the discretion to vote the shares. A broker &#8220;non-vote&#8221; will be counted for purposes of calculating whether a quorum is present at the 2026 Annual Meeting. However, broker &#8220;non-votes&#8221; will not be counted for purposes of determining the number of votes present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote with respect to a particular nominee or proposal as to which that broker &#8220;non-vote&#8221; occurs. Thus, a broker &#8220;non-vote&#8221; will not impact our ability to obtain a quorum for the 2026 Annual Meeting and will not otherwise affect the approval of Proposals One and Two.</span>

            <tr style="line-height:16.8pt;white-space:nowrap;text-align:left;vertical-align:top;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;font-variant:normal;text-transform:none;color:#000000;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">
              <td style="padding:0pt; width:0pt;">&#8203;</td>
              <td style="padding:0pt 0pt 0.5pt 0pt; width:24pt;">&#8203;</td>
              <td style="padding:0pt; width:3pt;">&#8203;</td>
              <td style="padding:0pt; width:3pt;">&#8203;</td>
              <td style="padding:6.3pt 0pt 1pt 0pt; width:457pt;white-space:normal;">
                <div style="line-height:11.8pt;">
                  <span style="letter-spacing:0.6pt;">Innisfree will, among other things, provide advice regarding proxy solicitation issues and solicit proxies from Tesla&#8217;s shareholders on Tesla&#8217;s behalf in connection with the 2026 Annual Meeting. For these and related advisory services, we will pay Innisfree a base fee of approximately $100,000 and a success fee in the event shareholders vote to approve Tesla&#8217;s proposals, in an amount determined by Tesla in its sole discretion, as well as reimburse them for certain out-of-pocket disbursements and expenses. The actual amount finally spent could be higher or lower depending on changing facts and circumstances in connection with this solicitation.</span>
                </div>
              </td>
              <td style="padding:0pt; width:0pt;">&#8203;</td>
